Bumps [@simplewebauthn/browser](https://github.com/MasterKale/SimpleWebAuthn/tree/HEAD/packages/browser) from 13.3.0 to 14.0.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​simplewebauthn/browser's releases.

v14.0.0 - The one after they go quantum

The headlining feature of this release is @​simplewebauthn/server gaining support for passkeys using the ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87 PQC algorithms in supported runtimes. And in those same supported runtimes, SimpleWebAuthn will automatically encourage registration of ML-DSA-44 passkeys to future-proof Relying Parties as PQC-capable FIDO2 authenticators and credential managers start coming to market. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/advanced/server/pqc-ml-dsa-support for more info 🚀

Setting our sites on the browser, @​simplewebauthn/browser picks up a new sendSignal() method as a single method to call all of the WebAuthn Signal APIs. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/packages/browser#sendsignal for more info 🛜

As for breaking changes, the minimum supported version of Node has been raised to Node LTS 22.x and higher, and Deno v2.4.x and higher. Going forward, SimpleWebAuthn will more formally aim to support Node LTS releases through their Active and Maintenance windows as tracked on the Node.js Releases page, and aim to support Deno minor releases for up to one year after their release

That's not all, though. Continue reading for the full list of changes in this release! 🎉

Changes:

  • [server] The PQC ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, and ML-DSA-87 signature algorithms are now supported as passkey public key algorithms when the runtime supports them. In runtimes that support these PQC algorithms, generateRegistrationOptions() will include ML-DSA-44 as the most preferred public key algorithm during registration. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/advanced/server/pqc-ml-dsa-support for more info (#785, #794)

  • [browser] The new sendSignal() method offers a simple way to invoke the WebAuthn Signal APIs. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/packages/browser#sendsignal for more info (#778)

  • [browser] The new browserSupportsPasskeys() helper method performs more robust WebAuthn support detection by also checking for typical passkey-related WebAuthn features. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/packages/browser#browsersupportspasskeys for more info (#761)

  • [browser] The new getBrowserCapabilities() helper method wraps WebAuthn's getClientCapabilities() with additional feature detection checks when possible. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/packages/browser#getbrowsercapabilities for more info (#761)

  • [server] verifyAuthenticationResponse() accepts an optional new expectedTopOrigin argument that supports cross-origin authentication verification. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/advanced/server/cross-origin-support for more info (#773, h/t @​agektmr)

  • [server] MetadataService.initialize() accepts an optional new logger argument that can be used to capture MetadataService status output in a project-specific manner. See https://simplewebauthn.dev/docs/advanced/server/metadata-service#logging for more info (#765)

  • [server] The typing of transports in excludeCredentials when calling generateRegistrationOptions(), and allowCredentials when calling generateAuthenticationOptions(), has been updated to string[] to make it easier to call these methods (#776)

  • [server] "tpm" attestation verification is now more tolerant of variable casing in the TPM manufacturer IDs (#772)

  • [server] generateRegistrationOptions() and verifyRegistrationResponse() now use the same default list of allowed public key algorithms for supportedAlgorithmIDs (#791)

  • [server] The validateCertificatePath() helper now supports x5c arrays containing cross-signed certificates (#796)

Breaking Changes

  • [browser] [server] The minimum supported runtime versions have been increased to Node LTS 22.x and higher, and Deno v2.4.x and higher (#763)

v13.3.3

Changes:

  • [server] Updated MDS blob signature verification to support more algorithms (#788)
  • [server] Updated MetadataService to know about the new FIDO MDS blob trust anchor certificate (#789)

v13.3.2

This update fixes a CVSS v4 Low (2.0) security vulnerability identified in @​simplewebauthn/server. See the security advisory linked below for more information.

Changes:

  • [server] Fixed an issue with verifyRegistrationResponse() allowing a maliciously-crafted attestation statement's x5c to contain a self-signed "root certificate" instead of chaining back to an RP-specified trust anchor (GHSA-6hxq-p678-4hr2)

prs.title: Isolated Kubernetes build execution + execution settings UI
prs.body:
## Summary

Runs heavy App builds (`application.deploy`, `application.sdk_update`) in temporary Kubernetes pods with their own memory envelope while the scheduler stays warm for lightweight work. Placement is persisted at enqueue; the scheduler controller owns deterministic UID-bound Jobs with pod admission fencing, heartbeats, cancellation, timeouts, and cleanup — and never falls back silently to local execution.

Product surface: a Kubernetes badge on remote jobs (Diagnostics), a gated Settings → Kubernetes → Executions tab (per-type remote toggles + max-parallel-runs, defaults to the measured compilers), and a one-per-transition admin notice with an explainer modal. Supporting groundwork: trustworthy workflow memory recording, flexible request/limit pod memory, `max_concurrency=1` defaults on heavy candidates, per-type concurrency overrides in the claim path.

Related to #769 — broader elastic runtime policy/lane work stays open; this PR does not close it.

## Verification

- Backend unit: 198 passed (K8s stack, scheduler claims, placement, tripwires, boundaries, memory recording)
- Backend e2e (targeted): 14 passed (metrics, SDK update, reimport-memory)
- `quality api` (pyright + ruff): clean
- Client `tsc`/`lint`: clean; client unit (touched areas): 35 passed

prs.title: Per-profile AI model failover for transport-terminal errors
prs.body:
Fixes #784.

## What
Operator-configured fallback pointer on AI model profiles (`failover_profile_id`) so transport-terminal provider errors roll to another model/provider instead of failing the run. Failover fires only after the 6-attempt/60s transport budget is exhausted with a retryable identity (408/429/5xx, timeout, connection error). Everything else — 4xx, validation, token-limit truncation, budget, cancellation — stays terminal on the primary.

## How
- Migration + ORM self-FK (RESTRICT), cycle + max-3 validation, delete guard, merge successor repoint
- `resolve_chain` / `get_llm_configs`: skips unresolvable members (`ai_model_chain_skip`), raises head error when empty
- `FailoverModel`: per-request, sticky, per-candidate settings, streams establishment-only
- Executors + `PydanticAIClient` build observed chains; override/max-tokens primary-only; `failover_path` (JSON string) in run metadata; `ai_model_failover` log; usage per serving model
- Admin UI picker + badge + same-connection warning; regenerated types; policy-doc allowlist amendment

## Verification (focused; merge queue is the broad gate)
- `./test.sh unit`: 6435 passed
- e2e: failover pointer round-trip/guards, model settings, delegation lifecycle, workflow tools
- Client: new picker vitest, settings suites, `tsc`, `lint`, Playwright `ai-model-settings.admin.spec.ts`
- `./test.sh quality api`: pyright + ruff clean
- Live debug-stack runs on real cheap OpenRouter models: dead-endpoint skip, stub-500 request-time switch with recorded path, 404 negative control
- Production analysis motivating scope in #784 (90d ~1.3% failed, bursty upstream 429/connection errors)

Not run: full backend e2e suite, full Playwright suite, `./test.sh pre-pr` (leaving the broad gate to the merge queue).

## Notes for reviewers
- Same-connection fallback only covers single-model incidents; different connection/key needed for quota isolation (UI warns).
- Resolve-time skips log but do not write run metadata; request-time switches do both.
- Test-stack API has no hot reload: container restarts were needed between backend edits during development (local-only note).

prs.title: Supervised workflow services: control plane, worker mode, logs, UI, CLI
prs.body:
Ships the supervised-services milestone (plan: docs/plans/2026-09-20-supervised-workflow-services-plan.md, handoff: docs/plans/2026-09-21-services-completion-handoff.md).

**Scope**

prs.title: Gate table updates on both pre-image and post-image
prs.body:
Fixes #790

## Problem
Row `update` policy checks ran against the pre-image only. A user authorized to write a row (e.g. `row.organization_id == user.organization_id` matches their own org) could mutate it into a value they should never be able to write — e.g. retarget `organization_id` to another org — because the target value was never policy-checked.

## Change
Require the `update` action on BOTH the pre-image and the post-image (merged for PATCH / `merge_upsert` / `upsert=true`, replaced for single `upsert` / `replace_upsert`). Either failure → 403, row untouched.
- `api/src/routers/tables.py`: new `_check_update_or_403` (single policy load, single deny audit, same commit contract as `_check_action_or_403`); wired into `update_document`, `insert_document` upsert branch, `upsert_document`. Existing `create` checks kept as-is (strictly stricter, no loosening).
- `api/shared/table_batch_writes.py`: new `_update_post_image_row` builder (column-mapped `id`/`table_id`/`created_by`/`created_at` always win, matching `_row_from_doc`); `_check_policies` denies when either image fails. Shared with the router so both layers agree on the post-image shape.
- Inserts (`create` on candidate) and deletes (`delete` on pre-image) are unchanged.

## Behavior note
With row-state-only rules, allowing a transition INTO a state also allows edits WITHIN it (rules see the post-image, not the transition). `test_state_locked_update` was reworked accordingly: status transitions still succeed when the update rule ignores the transitioning field, and read-gating remains the opt-in "self-hide" mechanism.

## Verification (worktree `790-table-policy-dual-gate`, per-worktree test stack)
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_policies.py` — 25 passed (rewrote `test_update_gates_on_pre_image_only` → `test_update_gates_on_both_pre_and_post_image`; added `test_cannot_retarget_organization_id_via_patch`, `..._via_upsert`, `test_batch_upsert_cannot_retarget_organization_id`; reworked `test_state_locked_update`)
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_tables_batch.py tests/e2e/platform/test_tables.py tests/unit/test_table_bulk_upsert_route.py tests/unit/test_table_batch_contract.py tests/unit/routers/test_tables_batch.py tests/unit/policies/test_probe.py` — 91 passed
- `./test.sh quality api` — pyright + ruff clean

prs.title: Consolidate redundant backend E2E setup
prs.body:
## Summary

Consolidates repeated backend E2E work while preserving distinct live contracts. Solution capture, secrets, storage, reinstall, table routing, cascade, and file isolation use direct service or DB setup where a second worker job adds no coverage. A single healthy service lifecycle covers claim, ready, logs, scoped token, event emission, restart, and stop; a separate crash path remains. Workspace config input/encryption, app publish/deduplication, and CLI app CRUD/dependencies each share their relevant job or lifecycle. A network-backed package-update assertion is replaced by deterministic parser/response tests plus an authorization E2E check.

The final pass combines connection template capture, shell creation, README, ZIP install, and exact binary asset bytes in one Solution deploy and one install. That consolidation exposed and fixes a real export defect: a README edited through `PUT /readme` was omitted from shareable ZIPs when a deploy-time source artifact existed. Both shareable and full export now place the current README over the immutable stored source.

CI allocates E2E files across three isolated runners by source size, without a maintained timing map. The required aggregate `E2E Tests` check remains unchanged. The branch also codifies the expensive-test review rule, fixes Git workspace sync-down of stale files, and moves the test/debug SeaweedFS admin port outside the Linux ephemeral range.

## Measured cost

| Candidate | Complete CI wall | E2E shard jobs | Pytest shard times |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Recent main `74b8dd5ab` | 24:28 | 24:18 / 12:56 | 21:46 / 10:30 |
| This branch, two shards `0bab77214` | 12:49 | 8:52 / 12:40 | 6:37 / 10:01 |
| **This branch, three shards `202b5e470`** | **9:29** | **6:31 / 8:36 / 9:20** | **4:34 / 6:02 / 7:38** |

Main and branch runs differ in test content and runner conditions, so this table measures the whole PR's observed effect rather than attributing every minute to sharding. The two-to-three-shard change reduced the observed branch CI wall by 3:20. The last full local sequential backend E2E run before the final pass was 1,854 passed in 22:08; the final head's complete CI E2E run passed 1,812 tests with 39 skips across three shards.

prs.title: Retry safe SDK POST calls after transient platform disconnects
prs.body:
## Incident evidence

The 2026-09-24 execution review found 32 `ReadError` and three `ConnectTimeout` failures across multiple workflows. Traces show 26 calls to SDK reads or named table writes that made only one attempt because their POST/PATCH methods lack an idempotency opt-in. Separate Kubernetes evidence shows API readiness timeouts on a CPU-saturated node; infrastructure placement is addressed in gocovi/kubernetes#6.

## Change

- Opt read-only POST calls (`tables.query`, integration get/list/get_mapping, knowledge search) into the existing transient transport and 502/503/504 retry policy.

- Leave `workflows.execute` single-attempt because a retry could dispatch duplicate work. A request idempotency key is needed before making dispatch retryable.

Filtered `tables.count` already delegates to `tables.query`; unfiltered count uses GET and already retries.

prs.title: fix(agents): parse structured output wrapped in a markdown code fence
prs.body:
## Why

When `agents.run(..., output_schema=...)` is used, `AutonomousAgentExecutor.run` parses the final reply with a bare `json.loads`. Models asked for JSON often wrap it in a markdown code fence:

````
```json
{"result": 42}
```
````

The parse fails, the executor keeps the raw string, and the agent-run consumer stores it as `{"text": "```json\n{...}\n```"}`. The SDK only re-parses string outputs, so the caller gets the envelope dict back instead of the parsed object. Any caller that treats "got a dict" as "got the schema object" then silently sees missing fields.

We hit this after switching the default profile to a newer model, which fences structured replies much more often than the previous one (every run, in our testing, for one agent that previously parsed cleanly).

#796 already unwraps `{"text": ...}` for runs **without** an `output_schema`. This covers the schema case at the source, so the stored run output and every caller get the parsed object.

## What

- New module-level helper `_parse_structured_output()` in `autonomous_agent_executor.py`: strips one outer code fence (with or without a language tag), then `json.loads`. Anything that is not a bare or fenced JSON document is returned unchanged, exactly as before (prose around a fence is deliberately not guessed at).
- The `output_schema` parse in `run()` uses it.

## Tests

`api/tests/unit/services/test_autonomous_agent_executor.py`: parametrized cases for bare, ```` ```json ````, bare ```` ``` ````, and whitespace-padded fences; non-JSON and prose-plus-fence inputs come back unchanged. The file passes (43 tests) and `ruff` is clean on the touched files.

Note: I could not run the full `./test.sh pre-pr` gate on this machine; only the targeted unit tests and ruff were run.

prs.title: feat(ai): add OpenCode Go as a supported AI provider
prs.body:
## Why

OpenCode Go (https://opencode.ai/docs/go) does not work through the existing "OpenAI-compatible" option. Its docs ask every client to identify itself and to send a session header (x-opencode-session) for each conversation, and its models are spread across three different endpoints - which a single OpenAI-compatible connection could express.

## What changed

- Adds a first-class `opencode_go` provider kind with the documented endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`:
  - `AIProviderKind` contract, ORM check constraint, and alembic migration (downgrade supported).
  - Provider dropdown entry and regenerated client types.
- Routes each model to the surface Go documents for it:
  - `/chat/completions` - the bulk of the catalog (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, Hy3, LongCat, …)
  - `/responses` - Grok 4.x, GPT 6 Luna, GPT 5.6 Luna, Muse Spark
  - `/messages` - MiniMax, Qwen (Anthropic client based at `/zen/go`, since its SDK re-appends `/v1/messages`; Go requires the key as `x-api-key` there)
  - Unlisted models default to chat completions.
- Sends `User-Agent: Bifrost/<version>` and `x-opencode-session` on agent runs, direct LLM clients (`ai.complete`/`ai.stream`), and provider catalog calls. Sessions are conversation ids for chat, run ids for autonomous runs, and a stable per-client id for direct calls.
- Keeps the legacy plain `max_tokens` wire field for Go's DeepSeek models (existing DeepSeek-family guard).
- Reuses the adaptive Anthropic prompt-cache fallback for the Messages surface.

## Sensitive paths

- **Migration** (`20260924_opencode_go_provider`): widens the `ck_ai_provider_connections_provider` check constraint. Chained onto the current head so the revision graph stays linear; downgrade restores the previous constraint.
- **API contract**: `AIProviderKind` gains a value. No CLI/SDK-consumed DTO shapes changed (`test_contract_version.py` and `test_dto_flags.py` pass unchanged).

## Verification

Backend (Dockerized test stack):
- `./test.sh tests/unit/services/test_opencode_go.py tests/unit/services/test_agent_runtime.py tests/unit/test_ai_model_service.py tests/unit/services/test_provider_catalog_service.py tests/unit/test_ai_model_profiles_migration.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py tests/unit/test_contract_version.py -v` → 140 passed
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/test_ai_model_settings_api.py -v` → 4 passed (includes a new opencode_go connection/profile round trip)
- `./test.sh quality api` → Pyright 0 errors, ruff clean

Client:
- `npm run tsc` → exit 0
- `npm run lint` → 0 errors (one pre-existing warning in `e2e/support/seed-review-pack.ts`)
- `npm run generate:types` against the running dev stack → provider unions match this change

Live gateway validation against OpenCode Go (real key):

- Direct minimal probes (prompt "hi", output capped at 4–16 tokens each): `mimo-v2.6-flash` and `deepseek-v4.1-flash` (plain `max_tokens`) over `/chat/completions`; `gpt-6-luna` over `/responses`; `qwen3.8-flash` over `/messages` (key as `x-api-key`).
- End-to-end through Bifrost: connection plus profiles for all three surfaces, each answered in Chat; `ai_usage` rows recorded as `provider = opencode_go`.
- Happy to provide a key privately if you'd like to try it during review - I didn't want to paste one into a public PR.

## Known limitations

- Wire routing is prefix-based on Go's published catalog (cross-checked against all 42 live model ids). A future responses/messages-only model with a new prefix would default to chat completions until the mapping is extended.
- OpenCode Go publishes no pricing catalog, so its usage rows have `cost = NULL` and the existing "AI Model Missing Pricing" admin notification fires; prices can be entered manually.
- Connection verification can list Go's catalog but cannot validate the key, because Go's `/models` endpoint is public (same behaviour as OpenRouter).

Closes #806 This is my first PR here, so I'm happy to adjust anything.

prs.title: Restore audit attribution and error parity on the worker SDK socket
prs.body:
Follow-up to #810 (post-merge review).

## Problem
#810 serves SDK routes to execution children from a bare FastAPI app on a worker-local Unix socket. That app lacked the API's request-context middleware and global exception handlers:

- `emit_audit` skips silently without an actor, so user/role/organization mutations and file/table policy denials made from workflows stopped being audited (before #810 they were recorded as the engine sentinel).
- `IntegrityError` / `ValueError` / `NoResultFound` / `OperationalError` returned plain 500s over the socket. Example: concurrent table auto-create returns 409 over HTTP (which the SDK treats as success) but 500 over the socket, failing `sdk.tables.insert`.

## Change
- `src/core/app_wiring.py`: the exception handlers and request-context middleware move out of `main.py` (unchanged behavior and ordering) and are installed on both the API app and the worker socket app.
- **Workflow SDK actions are attributed to the execution's caller.** `mint_engine_token` emits signed `engine_caller_*` claims from the consumer's known caller. They are read only by `src/core/request_actor.py::actor_from_token_payload`. `sub`, `is_superuser`, `UserPrincipal` and every authorization decision are unchanged. Runs without a human caller record the system user; service tokens record `source="service"`.
- `audit_logs.execution_id` (nullable UUID, indexed, no FK because service attempt ids are not executions and executions are retention-deleted). It is exposed on the audit list response with an `execution_id` filter.
- `sdk_ai`: restore the sanitized 500 "AI completion failed" for non-`ValueError` client-resolution failures.
- `sdk_knowledge`: remove the uncalled pre-embedded helpers and correct the docstring.
- Unchanged by decision: the external-caller org-only OAuth refresh from #810, which extends the existing global-secrets carve-out for external users. It is covered by `test_cli_integrations_external.py::test_external_cannot_refresh_global_provider`.

prs.body:
Tightens several endpoints to match the platform's access rules. Only platform-org principals manage platform data, and credentials reach only real executions.

## Changes
- **SDK credential and admin routes:** `/api/sdk/config/*`, `/api/sdk/integrations/*`, the knowledge write routes (`store`, `store-many`, `delete`, namespace delete) and `/api/sdk/tables/{create,list}` now require `CurrentEngineOrBypassUser`. Applies the platform access rule to write paths and MCP tools. Regular (non-bypass) users change nothing platform-managed except their own private agents, and see only agent runs they started. Bypass means platform admin or provider-org member (`has_scope_bypass`).

## REST
- **Apps** (`applications.py`, `app_code_files.py`): every mutation (create, update, delete, draft, publish, replace, swap-slugs, rollback, logo, source file write/delete, dependencies) is bypass-only. Denials keep the existing not-found response.
- **MCP connections** (`mcp_connections.py`): org-level connection writes (create, update, delete, tool toggle, tool refresh, service-token connect) are bypass-only. Per-user `/api/me/...` credentials are unchanged.
- **Agent tuning** (`agent_tuning.py`): bypass, or the owner of a private agent.
- **Agent runs** (`agent_runs.py`, `agent_run_access.py`, `shared/sdk_agent_runs.py`):
  - Non-bypass callers see only runs they started. Delegated children are visible when their parent run is the caller's.
  - Tuning actions (rerun, verdicts, flags, dry run) are limited to the caller's own runs of their own private agent. Cancel stays own-run.
  - `/execute` and `/enqueue` resolve the agent through the standard access check.
- **Forms repository:** `get_form_with_access_check` gains the platform-admin fast path that the agent repository already has.

## MCP tools, now matching REST
- `create_agent`, `create_form` and the organization tools are now thin REST wrappers.
- `get_agent` and `get_form` use the REST access checks.
- `update_form`, the table-metadata tools, `register_workflow` and the event tools are platform-admin only, matching their `CurrentSuperuser` REST routes.
- The app tools, `push_files` and the code-editor tools (reads and writes) are bypass-only.

prs.title: Enforce own-scope visibility for runs, artifacts, channels and admin reads
prs.body:
Applies the platform access rule to read paths. Regular (non-bypass) users see only their own agent runs, their own artifacts, and data they're granted. Admin internals stay admin-only.

## Changes
- **WebSocket channels** (`websocket.py`):
  - `agent-run:{id}` is limited to the run's caller or bypass principals.
  - The shared `agent-runs` and `event-source:{id}` channels are bypass-only.
  - `app:draft:{id}` is bypass-only.
  - `app:live:{id}` uses the same access check as the REST app read.
  - `cli-session:{id}` is owner-only, and `git:{id}` is admin-only (nothing publishes to it).
- **Client:** `useAgentRunUpdates` subscribes to the per-run channel on the run detail page, so users keep live updates for their own runs. List views for non-admins rely on their existing refetch.
- **Artifacts** (`services/artifacts.py`): regular users list, read and resolve only artifacts they created. Storing into another user's workspace is refused. Bypass uses `has_scope_bypass`.
- **`/api/metrics`:** recent failures are scoped to the caller's org, and ROI is returned only to bypass callers. The dashboard keeps working, since `roi_24h` is already optional.
- **`/api/mcp-servers/{id}`:** non-bypass callers see only their own org's connections.
- **Knowledge:** fetching a document by id enforces own-org-or-global for non-bypass callers.
- **Agents** (`agents.py`):
  - Run stats (`/stats`, `include_stats`, fleet) count only the caller's own runs for non-bypass callers, never platform-wide.
  - `accessible-tools` and `accessible-knowledge` filter role grants to the caller's org.
  - Private agents are readable only by their owner or a platform admin.
  - Each delegation is access-checked.
- **Other reads:**
  - `GET /api/integrations/{id}/logo` is admin-only.
  - A bundle-manifest GET no longer triggers a build for non-bypass callers.

Not changed: embed token behavior, table-document denial codes, SDK knowledge read semantics, and `/api/tools`.

## Tests

RBAC R1b, agents batch (program: `docs/plans/2026-09-26-rbac-program-handoff.md`, triage: `docs/plans/2026-09-26-r1-domain-triage.md`).

- **MCP agent tools are now thin REST wrappers.** `api/src/services/mcp_server/tools/agents.py` no longer touches the ORM; list/get/create/update/delete call `/api/agents` through the in-process HTTP bridge, so MCP enforces exactly what REST enforces. Name refs resolve through the shared `RefResolver` (same as the CLI).
- **Tool renames (user-visible):** `list_agents` → `bifrost_agent_list`, `get_agent` → `bifrost_agent_get`, `create_agent` → `bifrost_agent_create`, `update_agent` → `bifrost_agent_update`, `delete_agent` → `bifrost_agent_delete`. Migration `20260927_agent_mcp_names` rewrites stored `agents.system_tools` entries (tested against Postgres on a seeded agent).
- **Catalog naming:** all 99 catalog MCP names flip to `bifrost_<noun>_<verb>` (metadata only outside agents). The catalog now validates the pattern, a closed verb set, length ≤ 64 and uniqueness; a test asserts the registered agent tools equal the catalog names (`CANONICAL_MCP_DOMAINS = {"agents"}`, extended per batch).
- **REST agent writes: applied or refused, never silently ignored.** New `api/src/services/agent_write_policy.py`. Non-admins get 403 instead of silent drops/overrides; everyone gets 422 for invalid references.
- **Agent editor:** non-admins no longer send, or see controls for, admin-only fields.

## Persona × behavior decision table — please approve each changed row

PA = platform admin · PO = provider-org member, not admin · OM = regular org member · EXT = external user. "Admin" for agent writes stays `is_platform_admin` (unchanged).

### MCP

| # | Tool | Persona | Before | After (= REST) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | list | PA | own org + global only, role-filtered like a regular user | all agents in all orgs; `scope` filters |
| 2 | list | PO, OM, EXT | cascade + role filter + own private | unchanged |
| 3 | list / get | all | trimmed custom dict | full `AgentSummary` / `AgentPublic` |
| 4 | get by id | PO | could read another user's private agent | 404 unless owner |

prs.title: feat(mcp): preserve separated discovery documents
prs.body:
Supersedes #766 by @MTG-Thomas (the contributor organization blocks maintainer pushes). Thomas's commit is kept as authored.

OAuth discovery for MCP servers keeps the authorization-server and protected-resource documents under separate keys, and flattens only an allowlist of resource-scoped fields, so a protected-resource document can no longer replace the authorization server's issuer or endpoints (RFC 9728). Protected-resource metadata is fetched from the path-aware URL.

Added on top: fall back to the host-root `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` when the path-aware document is absent, as the MCP authorization spec (2025-11-25) requires, with a test for the ordering.

prs.title: fix(solutions): delete a failed from-repo install atomically with the job failure
prs.body:
Fixes a read-skew in from-repo Solution installs, found when `test_install_from_repo_rolls_back_on_deploy_failure` failed in the merge queue (run 36326161742).

**Bug:** when a from-repo install's first deploy failed, `_run_deploy_job` committed the deploy job's `failed` status in one transaction and `run_solution_deploy` deleted the new Solution row in a later one. Anything polling `GET /api/solutions/deploy-jobs/{id}` could see `failed` while `GET /api/solutions` still listed the orphan, and an immediate retry with the same slug hit a slug conflict.

**Fix:** `_run_deploy_job(..., delete_install_on_failure=True)` (passed only for `install_from_repo`) clears `job.install_id` and deletes the orphan in the same transaction as the `failed` status write. The later cleanup block in `run_solution_deploy` is removed: the deploy job's status is only written by `_run_deploy_job`/`_run_install_job`, so by the time it ran the row was always already gone.

**Tests:**
- New `test_run_deploy_job_deletes_orphan_in_same_transaction_as_failed_status` — reads back through a fresh session; fails on main (job failed, orphan still present), passes with the fix.
- `test_failed_repo_install_cleanup_commits_before_job_failure` rewritten to the new contract (the platform job still raises, and no longer touches the install).
- `./test.sh tests/unit/routers/test_solution_deploy_jobs.py tests/unit/jobs/test_solution_deploy_platform_job.py tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_install_from_repo.py` — 11 passed
- `./test.sh quality api` — clean

prs.title: fix(ci): Dependabot auto-merge actually enqueues; lockfile regen push triggers CI
prs.body:
## Summary

Two bugs in the Dependabot workflows. Only these two files change; nothing that builds or deploys is touched.

1. **Auto-merge never entered the merge queue** (`dependabot-auto-merge.yml`). `gh pr merge --auto --squash` on a merge-queue branch enables auto-merge but never enqueues (`gh pr merge --help`: on a merge-queue branch "no merge strategy is required"). This stranded #786, #718 and #828 until someone ran `--disable-auto` + a bare `gh pr merge`. Dropped `--squash`; the "Protect Branch" ruleset's merge queue already sets `merge_method: SQUASH`.
2. **Regenerated `requirements.lock` never triggered CI** (`dependabot-lockfile-regen.yml`). Pushes made with `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't start workflow runs, so Python Dependabot PRs sat on stale checks. The push now uses a GitHub App installation token (`actions/create-github-app-token`, SHA-pinned). `workflow_dispatch` was rejected: GitHub's required-status-checks docs say dispatched runs on a PR head branch don't satisfy required checks. The misleading header comment ("CI re-runs") is corrected.

Hardening in the regen job, since `pip-compile` can execute sdist build code from the PR's dependency set:
- Checkout is read-only with `persist-credentials: false`.
- The container mounts only `pyproject.toml`, `requirements-piptools.lock` and `requirements.lock` in a temp dir — never the checkout or `.git` — so build code can't plant hooks or git config that would run during the push.
- The App token is minted only when the lock actually changed, scoped to this repo with `contents: write` only, and passed to a single `git push` via env as an `http.extraheader` (never persisted).
- Verified locally that regenerating with only those three files produces a byte-identical lock.

## Setup required (maintainer)

1. Create a GitHub App installed on `gobifrost/bifrost` with repository permission **Contents: Read and write** (nothing else).
2. Add two **Dependabot** secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Dependabot — not Actions secrets, which Dependabot-triggered runs cannot read): `DEPENDABOT_LOCKFILE_APP_ID`, `DEPENDABOT_LOCKFILE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`.

Until they exist, the regen job fails with an explicit error — only when there is a lock change to push. It is not a required check.

## Behavior change

Eligible Dependabot PRs (security advisories at any level; patch/minor non-Docker version bumps) will now merge on their own once CI and the full merge-queue suite pass — the policy already documented in the workflow header. Majors and Docker image bumps still need review. Production is unaffected: `:latest`/prod only move on a manual `v*` tag.

Known, pre-existing consequence: once any non-Dependabot actor pushes to a Dependabot branch, Dependabot stops auto-rebasing that PR (`@dependabot recreate` if it conflicts).

## Verification

- `rhysd/actionlint` clean on both files.
- Local regen with only the three mounted files: identical `requirements.lock`.
- End-to-end proof is the first Python Dependabot PR after the secrets are set, and the first eligible PR entering the queue unassisted.

- REST: the nine CLI-session routes under `/api/sdk/sessions…`, their 10 DTOs, `CLISessionRepository`, the `CLISession` model.
- WebSocket: `local-runner:`, `devrun:`, `cli-session(s):` channels and the pubsub publishers (the `devrun`/local-runner-state layer had zero callers).

Only explicit opt-in callers ever sent it; `excludeLocal` is now an unknown parameter (422), pinned by a test.

prs.title: System account never holds roles; agent tool picker lists only usable tools
prs.body:
## Summary

**1. The system account can never be assigned a role.** Embedded-app and engine execution act as the platform's system account, and some access checks read that account's role memberships, so it should never have any.
- New `shared/system_account_guard.py`, called from every writer of `user_roles`:
  - `POST /api/roles/{id}/users` (shared `sdk_roles.assign_users_to_role`, used by REST, CLI, MCP and the workflow SDK) → **422** "The system account can't be assigned roles".
  - `PATCH /api/users/bulk` `replace_roles` → the system account lands in the response's `failed[]` (that endpoint's existing partial-success contract; it was already refused by its `is_system` check).
  - Workflow write-buffer role flush (`bifrost/_sync.py`) → raises.
- Migration `20260927_no_sys_role`: `CHECK (user_id <> '<system account id>')` on `user_roles`, after deleting any such rows. Production was checked read-only first: **0** rows.
- Checked and not writers: git-sync/manifest import, Solution deploy, SSO/user provisioning, seeding.

**2. `/api/tools` (the agent editor's tool picker) lists only tools the caller can use.** Before, non-admins saw every tool workflow in their org + global, and saving an agent then rejected the ones they couldn't use. Now the list and the save check share one rule (`shared/workflow_access.py::user_can_access_workflow`), so they can't drift. Two extra queries per list call, no N+1.

## What changes for each kind of user (tool picker)

| Who | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Platform admin | every tool workflow in scope | unchanged |
| Provider-org member, regular org member | every tool in own org + global | only tools at `everyone` / `authenticated`, or `role_based` where they hold a matching role |
| External user | every tool in own org + global | only `everyone` tools, or `role_based` with a matching role (the `authenticated` tier never grants externals, matching the execute rule in `OrgScopedRepository`) |

Saving an agent behaves as before, with one alignment: an external user holding a role attached to an `authenticated`-level workflow could previously attach it; the execute path already refused them, and now the save check does too.

## Verification

- `./test.sh unit` — 7525 passed.
- `./test.sh e2e` — 1938 passed, 1 failed: `test_external_users.py::TestExternalToolsCatalog` asserted the old "externals list every global tool" behavior. Restated as two tests (visible at `everyone`, hidden at `role_based` without a role); that file + `test_tools.py` + new `test_tools_access_filter.py`: 32 passed.
- Migration applied on a fresh stack and round-tripped (`downgrade -1` / `upgrade head`); single Alembic head.
- `./test.sh quality api` clean.

**Tables**
- **Move a table between orgs / to global** (platform admin): `TableUpdate.organization_id` (omitted = unchanged, `null` = global, UUID = that org). `bifrost tables update --org <org> | --global` and MCP `bifrost_table_update`. Before, only the old MCP tool could do this; REST, CLI and UI couldn't. Policies are re-validated against the new org; audit records old and new org. The web table dialog never sends the field.
- Nonexistent target org → 422 on create/update. A name clash in the target scope → **409** (the repository never actually checked for this before; the router's handler couldn't fire).

**Events**
- New admin-only `GET /api/events/sources/{source_id}/subscriptions/{subscription_id}` (catalog `events.subscriptions.get`); `bifrost events get-subscription` uses it.

- **Subscription targets:** target must exist (404) and be an active workflow (not a `service`) or active agent (422); duplicate subscription → 409. An **org-scoped** source may only target its own org or global targets. A **global** source may target any org — production has 25 of 95 subscriptions that route a global source to org-level workflows/agents, so the reference's "global source → global targets only" rule was not adopted. Invalid-target responses are 422 throughout (the service-target case was 400).
- **Webhook resubscribe on change:** changing a source's webhook adapter, integration or adapter config subscribes the new registration at the provider first, then unsubscribes the old. If the new subscribe fails, the request fails (502) and nothing is changed; if unsubscribing the old fails, it's logged and the update succeeds.

All form/table/event **writes** and all table/event **reads** were platform-admin only on REST before and after. MCP now enforces exactly that.

| Who | Before (MCP) | After |
|---|---|---|
| Platform admin | full access; could move tables only via MCP | full access; table moves on REST/CLI/MCP; new get-subscription and delete-form tools |
| Provider-org member, regular org member, external user | forms list/get: own org + global, role-filtered; everything else refused | unchanged — same results now come from REST |

prs.title: MCP workflows/apps tools: canonical names + thin REST wrappers; app management platform-admin only (RBAC R1b batch 5)
prs.body:
## Summary

RBAC R1b, batch 5 — the last R1b domain batch. Same shape as #830 / #833 / #834.

- **MCP tools renamed to catalog names and made thin REST wrappers:**
  - workflows: `bifrost_workflow_{list,get,validate,register,update,delete,execute}`, `bifrost_workflow_role_{grant,revoke}` — including `execute_workflow` → `bifrost_workflow_execute`, the most commonly attached agent tool.
  - apps: `bifrost_app_{list,get,create,update,publish,replace,validate}`, `bifrost_app_dependencies_{get,update}`, plus new `bifrost_app_delete`. `push_files` keeps its name (no catalog op).
- **New `GET /api/workflows/{workflow_id}`** (platform-admin only, catalog `workflows.get`); `bifrost workflows get` uses it. No name cascade on id lookup, so admins can read any org's workflow by id.
- **App management is platform-admin only.** Create, update, delete, publish, replace, rollback, slug swap, logo, dependencies, V1 draft/file writes, and MCP `push_files` previously allowed platform admins *or provider-org members*; V2 deploy and SDK update were already admin-only. Everyone keeps read/use access to the apps they can see.
- Audit events on workflow register/update/delete/role grant/revoke and app create/update/delete/publish/replace/dependencies update.
- Migration `20260928_r1b_mcp_names_b5` renames stored ids in `agents.system_tools` and the platform MCP allow/block lists — agents with `execute_workflow` attached keep working.

## What changes for each kind of user

| Who | Workflows via MCP | Apps (REST, CLI, MCP) |
|---|---|---|
| Platform admin | unchanged; new get-by-id | unchanged |
| Provider-org member (not admin) | list/get: **before** org + global rows (no role filter) · **after** refused (403), same as REST. Execute unchanged (role-checked) | **before** could create/edit/delete/publish apps · **after** view/use only |
| Regular org member, external user | list/get: **before** org + global rows · **after** refused. Execute unchanged | view/use only (unchanged) |

Also: MCP `bifrost_app_create` now follows REST's rule that app slugs are globally unique, so it refuses a slug already used by a Solution install (the old MCP tool skipped that check).

## Verification

- `./test.sh unit` — 7516 passed (after replacing 10 unit tests of the removed MCP app internals: the wrappers are tested to forward REST's Solution-managed 409, REST's guards are covered by `test_solution_readonly_full.py`, and slug resolution is the shared `ApplicationRepository.get_by_slug_global`; plus one fixture that lacked the app `name` now read by the audit call).
- `./test.sh e2e` — 1980 passed, 1 failed: the publish-dedupe test used a provider-org member as its second publisher. It now uses a second platform admin for the dedupe check and asserts the provider-org member gets 404; re-run: 2 passed.
- New: workflow list 403 for non-admins, workflow get (admin cross-org, non-admin 403, 404), execute for an org member with a role-granted workflow via MCP and REST, app CRUD parity, provider-org app write refusals (router + `push_files`), migration real-Postgres up/down.
- `./test.sh quality api`; client `tsc`; `v1.d.ts`, inventory, skill appendices and Codex mirrors regenerated.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

No user facing changes.

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

4.37.5 - 03 Aug 2026

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

4.37.4 - 29 Jul 2026

  • This version of the CodeQL Action adds support for the tools input for the codeql-action/init step to be specified using a github-codeql-tools repository property. This feature will gradually be rolled out following the release of this version. Once rolled out, this allows for the CodeQL CLI version that is used in GitHub-managed workflows, such as Default Setup, to be set to a custom value. For example, customers who run into issues with rate limits when a new CodeQL CLI version is released can set the value to toolcache to always use the CodeQL CLI version that is available in the runner toolcache. For Advanced Setup workflows, the value provided for tools in the workflow definition always takes precedence unless the value of the repository property starts with !. #4037

prs.title: fix(ci): run Dependabot auto-merge and lockfile push as the GitHub App
prs.body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #829, whose two fixes were necessary but not sufficient (observed on the first real Dependabot run today).

**1. Auto-merge never entered the merge queue.** Dependabot PRs were merged automatically by `github-actions` from April until **2026-06-10** (#71…#365). The merge queue was added to `main` that day (ruleset history), and every Dependabot merge since was manual. Today #839/#842 sat green with auto-merge enabled by the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` and never queued; running `gh pr merge` as a person queued them immediately. Events caused by `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't start new workflow runs, and queue membership depends on a `merge_group` run. **Fix:** the eligible-PR step now mints a `bifrost-lockfile-bot` App token (Contents + Pull requests: write) and runs `gh pr merge --auto` with it. Labelling majors/Docker stays on `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the job's own token drops to `contents: read`.

**2. The regenerated `requirements.lock` push got HTTP 403** (#837). A freshly minted token for the same App can create branches and push new commits here (verified with throwaway branches), so the failure was specific to the hand-built `http.extraheader` push from the first checkout. **Fix:** after the credential-free regen step, a second `actions/checkout` into `push-tree/` holds the App token as its standard persisted credential (the pattern `actions/create-github-app-token` documents), commits the copied lock, and pushes. The untrusted `pip-compile` still runs with no credentials anywhere in reach.

Policy is unchanged: security bumps (any level) and patch/minor non-Docker bumps auto-merge after CI + the full merge-queue suite; majors and Docker images get `needs-review`. Production still only moves on a manual `v*` tag.

## Verification

- `actionlint` clean on both files.
- End-to-end proof after merge: `@dependabot recreate` on #837 → the regen push must land and trigger CI, and the eligible PRs must enter the queue on their own. Not claimed until observed.

prs.title: Engine tokens: not persisted in diagnostic context, redacted from output, end with their execution
prs.body:
## Summary
Hardens the per-execution engine token lifecycle. No change to what any user can do.

- **Not persisted:** the diagnostic Redis copy of an execution context (`bifrost:exec:{id}:context`, read by queue display) no longer includes `engine_token`. The child still receives the full context over its private work pipe. Other stored context fields were inventoried; none carry credentials. Agent-run contexts never held a token.
- **Redacted:** the child registers the engine token as an execution secret, so `_scrub_outputs` and log-line redaction replace it with `[REDACTED]` in results, logs, variables and error messages.
- **Ends with its execution:** `get_current_user_optional` rejects an execution-scoped engine token (superuser + `engine_execution_id`) unless that execution's row in Postgres is Pending, Running or Cancelling (`LIVE_EXECUTION_STATUSES` in `models/enums.py`, checked by the new `shared/execution_liveness.py::is_execution_live`, one primary-key lookup). A DB error fails closed. Supervised-service tokens (non-superuser) are unaffected.

The first version read liveness from the Redis active-execution lease; the merge queue caught that `test_running_execution_completes_after_redis_tracking_loss` deletes that lease mid-run by design, so the lease is not an authoritative signal. The DB status is.

Tests that mint engine tokens directly now create a real live execution row (`tests/helpers/live_execution.py`).

## Verification
- Full `./test.sh unit`: 7541 passed, 0 failed
- Full `./test.sh e2e`: 1982 passed, 0 failed
- `test_running_execution_completes_after_redis_tracking_loss`: 13/13 consecutive passes

prs.title: RBAC R2a: tag audit rows with operation ID and surface; count per-workflow operation usage
prs.body:
## Summary
Second R2a slice. Attribution and measurement only — **no change to who can do what.**

**Audit rows**
- `audit_logs.operation_id` (catalog operation id of the matched route, NULL for uncatalogued routes) and `audit_logs.surface` (`web`, `cli`, `mcp`, `embed`, `workflow`, `service`). `source` keeps its meaning (actor type).
- Surface: engine token → `workflow`, service token → `service`, embed session → `embed`, else the self-reported `X-Bifrost-Surface` header (`cli`/`mcp`, attribution only), else `web`. The MCP thin-wrapper bridge sends `mcp`; the CLI/SDK non-engine HTTP clients send `cli`.
- Operation id is resolved when the row is written: the request-context middleware keeps the request's ASGI scope, and `emit_audit` reads `scope["route"]`. No FastAPI internals; identical on the main app and the worker-local SDK socket app.
- Both fields are in the audit log API response; client types regenerated.

**Per-workflow operation usage**
- `mint_engine_token` gains an `engine_workflow_id` claim (attribution only, never read for authorization).
- After each engine-token request, the middleware increments `bifrost:wf_usage:<day>` → `<workflow_id>|<operation_key>` in Redis (operation key = catalog id, else `METHOD /route/template`). Best effort: a Redis error never affects the response.
- A scheduler job flushes every 15 minutes into `workflow_operation_usage(workflow_id, operation_key, day, count)` with an additive upsert; deleted workflows are dropped.
- This is the data that will later show which permissions a workflow actually uses before anyone switches it to Restricted.

Migration `20260928_audit_op_surface` (down_revision `20260928_r1b_mcp_names_b5`, single head).

prs.title: Show cost, context, and cache rate per agent run
prs.body:
## Summary

Single-run agent surfaces headlined `tokens_used`. That number re-counts the whole conversation on every model call (cached tokens at full weight) and silently includes every delegate, so a run that never sent more than ~18k tokens in one request showed as 310k. Audited against production for 2026-09-28: all 41 root totals equalled their delegation subtree exactly — the arithmetic was right, the presentation was not — and the only wrong values were delegates that timed out or were cancelled, which recorded `0`.

### What a single run now shows

A new `usage_summary` on `AgentRunResponse` (list + detail), computed at read time from `ai_usage` and steps, so historical runs display correctly without a backfill:

- **Cost** — the whole run tree (delegates at any depth, plus the run summarizer), with the delegate share called out.
- **Peak context** — the largest single request in the run's own conversation (the closest analogue to a harness's "context used").
- **Cached** — share of input tokens read from the provider's prompt cache across the run tree.

Surfaces updated: agent run list/cards, review flipbook header, run detail AI Usage footer + card, advanced timeline (per call: `14.8k context · 0% cached`). Usage Reports keep their total-token view.

### Accounting fixes

- Delegates that time out or are cancelled now record their real `tokens_used` (the child executor's own counter), instead of a hard-coded `0`. Same for root runs killed by the consumer timeout.
- A delegate's total was `ledger_now − ledger_at_start` on the shared budget ledger, so concurrent sibling delegates would absorb each other's usage. Each executor now counts its own responses plus its delegates' subtree totals. The shared ledger still drives budgets, unchanged.

### Not in this PR

- Reasoning/effort per profile (separate PR).
- Token budget semantics (still counts cached tokens at full weight).
- Nothing provider-specific.

## Test plan

- `./test.sh tests/unit/services/test_agent_run_usage_summary.py tests/unit/services/test_autonomous_agent_executor.py tests/unit/services/test_agent_run_consumer.py` — 57 passed; the two new executor tests fail on the old executor.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_contract_version.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_agent_runs_service.py tests/unit/test_agent_run_response_includes_new_fields.py` — 82 passed (CLI contract fingerprint unchanged).
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_agent_run_usage_summary.py tests/e2e/api/test_agent_delegation_lifecycle.py tests/e2e/api/test_runs_search_and_filter.py` — all passed (lifecycle test's child-run mock now drives the executor counter like the real `run()`).
- `./test.sh quality api` clean; `npm run tsc` + `npm run lint` clean (5 pre-existing warnings in untouched files).
- Vitest: `src/lib/run-usage.test.ts`, `src/pages/agents`, `src/components/agents` — 439 + timeline passed.
- Drove the UI on a seeded dev stack (run list, run detail AI Usage, advanced timeline, review page).

prs.title: Use the models.dev catalog for providers, models, pricing, and reasoning
prs.body:
## Summary

Bifrost stops being special about model metadata. Like OpenCode, Hermes, and Cline, it now uses the [models.dev](https://models.dev) catalog (MIT, community-maintained) for the provider list, model lists, context windows, fallback prices, chat capabilities, and per-model reasoning options.

### Catalog lifecycle
- Trimmed snapshot shipped with the release (`model_catalog_snapshot.json.gz`, ~250 KB) — never empty, works offline.
- `model_catalog.refresh` platform job every 4 hours + at scheduler startup, with ETag; last good copy in the new `ai_model_catalog` table. Rejects responses with <20 providers or <50% of the last good model count (`catalog_rejected`); unreachable source fails retryably. Admin "Refresh catalog" button (`POST /api/admin/ai/catalog/refresh`, 202 + Location).

### Providers
- Provider picker lists ~200 catalog providers. **Native**: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenRouter, OpenCode Go. **Community**: every other provider whose catalog SDK maps onto a native adapter (`@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` → OpenAI-compatible, etc.), labelled "Community — not tested by Bifrost directly".
- Existing native connections on their standard endpoint are linked to the catalog by the migration; custom endpoints (e.g. Azure) stay custom and still list models from their own `/models`.
- Catalog OpenAI-compatible providers use Chat Completions without a transport probe.

### Models, pricing, capabilities
- Model pickers show context, price, and reasoning from the catalog; any model id can still be typed.
- A missing price is filled from the catalog for **any** provider on first use (insert-only — existing and hand-entered prices always win; provider-reported cost still wins per call). Pricing editor gains cache read/write price fields.
- Chat capabilities (image/PDF input, tools) come from the catalog unless an administrator record exists.

### Reasoning per profile
- New `reasoning_effort` on model profiles, validated against the model's catalog `reasoning_options` (effort levels, on/off toggle, or on/off for budget-only models). The control only appears when the catalog lists choices.
- Sent through each adapter's own field (`openrouter_reasoning`, `anthropic_effort`, `openai_reasoning_effort`, unified `thinking` for Google and toggles) because Pydantic AI's unified setting rounds levels (OpenRouter `xhigh`→`high`). Anthropic "on" sizes the thinking budget under the profile's output cap (found live: Anthropic rejects a budget ≥ max_tokens).
- Every call records `reasoning_tokens` (new `ai_usage` column); run AI Usage shows them inside output tokens.

### Removed
OpenRouter-specific model/media/pricing/capability lookups, the per-provider display-name registry (`model_registry.py`), the `/api/admin/llm/model-capabilities` endpoints, and two orphaned settings pages (`ModelCapabilityEditor`, `GenerationModelSettings`). Native usage rows keep their historical undated-id naming, so usage reports and prices don't split.

Runbook: `docs/runbooks/model-catalog.md`.

## Test plan

- Backend unit suite: `./test.sh unit` — 7,606 passed after fixes (new: catalog trim/parse/adapters/refresh safety, pricing fill-in, reasoning translation, service linking/validation, refresh job).

prs.title: Test saved model profiles with a real request and warn on failure
prs.body:
## Summary

Before #626, saving the AI config ran a real 1-token completion (`verify_completion`) because "a key may list models fine but be rejected on chat completions." #626 split the config into connections (no model) and profiles (connection + model). The completion check had nowhere to go and was dropped; only the `/models` listing survived. That listing proves little: Perplexity has no `/models`, DeepInfra and OpenRouter serve it without checking the key, and a working key can't catch a model it isn't allowed to call.

This PR restores the real check at the profile level:

- `POST /api/admin/ai/profiles/{profile_id}/verify` (platform admin) sends one short request ("Reply with the word OK.") through the profile's own runtime path: catalog routing, reasoning choice, output limit. It tests the profile alone, not its failover chain, and has a 30-second timeout. It returns `{success, message}` with the provider's error on failure.
- The UI calls it in the background after a profile is created or edited: in the settings create and edit dialogs, and in the profile selector's inline create. A failure shows a warning toast with the provider's error. **The save is not blocked or undone.** No other UI changes.
- There's no `max_tokens` cap on the check: Anthropic with reasoning on requires `max_tokens` above a thinking budget of at least 1,024 tokens, so the profile's own limit is used. The prompt is trivial, so cost is a fraction of a cent.

Connections keep their `/models` check.

## Verification

- Live, real keys (1Password): Anthropic `claude-haiku-4-5` default ✓; Anthropic with reasoning `on` ✓; OpenRouter `openai/gpt-5.4-nano` at `xhigh` ✓; OpenRouter `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` ✓; Anthropic bad key → 401 reported ✓; OpenRouter unknown model → 400 reported ✓. All rows rolled back.

## Summary

The scheduler's legacy logo-thumbnail backfill (#598) edited rows through the ORM and committed a whole batch at once. When a batch included a Solution-managed row, the always-on Solution write guard rejected the flush. The whole batch rolled back and was retried every minute, so nothing drained and the scheduler logged a traceback each run. The job also skipped forms and integrations.

prs.title: Workers and scheduler wait for the database schema before starting
prs.body:
## Summary

Migrations run once, in the API's init step. Nothing stopped the worker and scheduler from starting new code while the database was still on an older revision. When a migration failed during a rolling deploy, new workers ran queries against columns that didn't exist and failed real work until someone intervened. The fix lives in code, so it covers Kubernetes, Docker Compose and self-hosted installs alike.

- **`shared/schema_gate.py`:** `wait_for_schema` returns once the database is **at or ahead of** every Alembic head shipped with the image. A revision the image doesn't know counts as ahead, so an older image never blocks a rolling update. While the database is behind, it logs one warning per 5s poll naming current and expected revisions. After 15 minutes it raises, so the process exits non-zero and the orchestrator surfaces it.
- **Gated:** `Worker.start()` (before mappers and any RabbitMQ consumer; process-pool children don't poll) and `Scheduler.start()` (before heartbeat-dependent, diagnostics, platform-job and leadership tasks). The API and init are unchanged.
- **Alive but not ready while gated:**
  - The scheduler's liveness heartbeat keeps running while it waits.
  - Both processes write a ready marker only after the gate passes and their consumers or tasks have started.
  - New `python -m src.scheduler.health --ready` and `python -m src.worker.health --ready` checks read that marker. The existing `--max-age` liveness check is unchanged.
  - With a readiness probe, a stuck migration therefore pauses the rollout with the old pods still serving, instead of replacing them with pods that wait.
- **Compose:** worker and scheduler depend on `init: service_completed_successfully` and use `--ready` healthchecks. The dev/test/debug compose files mount `alembic/` and `alembic.ini` into worker and scheduler; the production image already ships them.
- **`k8s/`:** readiness probes on the worker and scheduler deployments.

Production manifests that live outside this repo should add:

```yaml
# bifrost-scheduler
readinessProbe:
  exec:
    command: ["python", "-m", "src.scheduler.health", "--ready"]
  periodSeconds: 10
  timeoutSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3
# bifrost-worker
readinessProbe:
  exec:
    command: ["python", "-m", "src.worker.health", "--ready"]
  periodSeconds: 10
  timeoutSeconds: 5
  failureThreshold: 3
```

## Verification

- `./test.sh quality api`: clean
- Schema gate (unit: fake revision graph with at-head / ahead / unknown / behind-then-advances / behind-past-max; e2e: `expected_heads()` equals `alembic heads`, migrated DB passes immediately), startup readiness, scheduler and worker health, worker startup lifecycle: 16 passed on current main

prs.body:
## Summary

The new authorization decision function, built next to today's checks and proven against them. **Nothing calls it from request handling.** No route, DTO or OpenAPI change.

- **`services/authorization/context.py`:** `AuthorizationContext` holds the base role, additional roles with their boundaries and permissions, and the External flag. It loads in three queries and deliberately doesn't carry the provider-org bypass flag.
- **`services/authorization/evaluator.py`:** `decide(ctx, entry, target)` → `Decision(allowed, rule)`.
  - A Platform Admin is allowed.
  - For `permission`-class operations, the permission must come from the base role (at the user's home org) or from a role whose boundary covers the target.
  - Non-permission classes are allowed for any signed-in user at their home org; `embed` is never a user decision.
  - Acting beyond one's own org needs a Platform Admin on an operation that allows it, or a covering role.
- **Access list:** new `AccessEntry.inline_effect` records what each inline check actually does: `deny_unless_superuser`, `deny_unless_bypass`, `widens_for_superuser`, `widens_for_bypass` or `no_caller_effect`. 255 entries were classified by reading their handlers. Misclassified entries are corrected to match today's behaviour (the OAuth connection routes, agent-run verdict and flag, `/ws/connect`, gateway capability search, `get_docs`), and several more provider-org paths now carry the standard `intended_change` marker.
- **User base role derivation fixed:** an MCP tool bound to a REST route is now judged by that route's entry, not by the MCP transport's signed-in floor, and routes whose handler refuses non-admins no longer count. The User set shrinks from 16 to 9 read permissions (removed: configs, events, integrations, policyrules, roles, tables, workflows). Migration `20260929_user_base_perm_fix` deletes those seeded rows. Nothing reads `role_permissions` at request time, so behaviour is unchanged.
- **Matrix (`tests/unit/authorization/test_decision_matrix.py`):** 740 entries × 5 personas (platform admin, provider-org member, regular, external, anonymous) × 3 targets (home org, another org, Global) = 11,100 cells.
  - Every cell must match a legacy oracle derived from today's gates.
  - The only exceptions are the listed differences (a provider-org member on entries carrying `intended_change`) and an explicit, per-entry pending set.

The 19 deferred management-read classifications will be resolved during R3 using the approved `.all` permission suffix and `reports` domain. This PR does not introduce that vocabulary or enforce authorization.

prs.title: Commit the request DB session before the response is sent
prs.body:
## Summary

`get_db` commits in the teardown of a `yield` dependency. On FastAPI 0.136.1, a default-scoped (`scope="request"`) yield dependency's teardown runs **after the response body has been sent**. An instrumented ASGI `send` shows `response body sent → dependency teardown (commit)`. Every route that relied on the implicit commit therefore returned 2xx before its write was committed:

- a client acting on the response right away could miss the row. This showed up as e2e flakes: a FK violation on an agent just created, a 404 on an MCP connection just created, "Table not found" on a table just created;
- if the commit itself failed, the client had already received a 2xx for a rolled-back write.

The fix uses FastAPI's `Depends(..., scope="function")`, whose teardown (commit, rollback, close) runs when the endpoint returns, before the response is sent:

- `DbSession` and `OptionalDbSession` (`core/db_deps.py`) and all 88 direct `Depends(get_db)` calls in 11 routers use `scope="function"`.
- The one route that used the request session after returning, the `cli_ai_stream` SSE generator, now opens its own session inside the generator. The other streaming, background and WebSocket paths were audited and don't use the request session after returning.
- Serialization after close is safe: sessions use `expire_on_commit=False`, so returned objects keep their loaded attributes. A lazy load during serialization already failed on an async session before this change, so there's no new failure mode.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/test_db_dependency_scope.py`: an AST guard that fails on any `Depends(get_db…)` without `scope="function"`, plus an instrumented-ASGI test asserting handler → commit → close → response body. Both fail if the scope is removed from `DbSession`.
- `tests/e2e/api/test_commit_before_response.py`: `POST /api/agents`, then immediately read the row through a separate connection.

## Verification

- `./test.sh quality api`: clean
- Targeted (scope guard and ordering, SDK AI stream, commit-before-response e2e, agent-run verdict, MCP connections): 47 passed on current main
- Implementer, on the final commit: full e2e 1991 passed, 0 failures; full unit green after the stream test was updated for the new, intended session ownership

prs.title: fix(agents): govern context by the model's real window, not a fixed 24k
prs.body:
## Problem

`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TARGET_TOKENS = 24_000` (from #597) was the context limit for every agent. It set both `WarnNearLimits(max_context_tokens=…)` and the `TieredCompaction` target, and nothing on an agent could change it. Any agent whose fixed input (system prompt, tools and task) is over 24k got this on every request after the first:

```
[WarnNearLimits]
CRITICAL: Configured run limits are approaching.
- Context window: 27207/24000 tokens used (113%); 0 remaining.
Complete the current task immediately and avoid unnecessary tool calls.
```

Compaction also tried to cut every request down to 24k. The Ticket Worker's fixed input is about 27k. It handed tickets back without delegating and said it had hit a "context limit". A replay with and without the warning showed it caused the change in outcome: 3/3 hand-backs with it, 3/3 delegations without.

## Change

- `build_runtime_capabilities` takes the model chain's real `context_window`. Compaction uses `target_fraction=0.5` and the warning uses `max_context_fraction=1.0`, so both are measured against that window.
- The new `chain_context_window` (in `model_pricing.py`) finds each candidate in the chain in the models.dev catalog and returns the smallest window. It returns `None` when the catalog knows none of them, and the harness then resolves the window itself.
- Both executors look up the window in the DB session they already open to resolve the LLM configs.
- Per-agent `max_iterations` / `max_token_budget` limits and the reserve for the final wind-down request behave exactly as before. That reserve was based on the old constant and is now its own named constant with the same value.
- The single-part clamp stays at 12k. The last-resort sliding window now keeps its default 40 messages instead of a tail of about 18k tokens.

## Tests

- `test_agent_runtime_context_window.py`:
  - A run whose first request reports 27k input tokens gets no warning and no compaction on a 200k window.
  - On a 30k window the warning is measured against 30k.
  - Both tests fail on `main` with the exact CRITICAL text above.
- `test_model_pricing.py`: `chain_context_window` returns the smallest known window, handles dated ids, returns `None` for unknown models, and applies the primary model override.
- Autouse fixture in `tests/unit/services/conftest.py`: executor unit tests run on mock sessions, so it treats the catalog window as unknown.

Commands run:
- `./test.sh quality api`: pyright and ruff clean.
- `./test.sh` on every unit test file that touches the executors, plus `test_model_pricing.py`, the new context-window test, and the wind-down tests: 157 passed.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_agent_delegation_lifecycle.py tests/e2e/api/test_agent_workflow_tool_execution.py`: 3 passed.

Not run: the full unit suite, the full e2e suite and `pre-pr`. The merge queue runs those.

## Worth knowing

- **Cost:** the bundled catalog lists the Claude Sonnet 4.5–5.5 models at 1M tokens, so on those models compaction now starts at about 500k instead of 24k. Agents with large inputs keep their full history, which is the point of the fix, but a long run with no `max_token_budget` can cost more per request than before.
- **Anthropic's 1M window:** Bifrost doesn't send Anthropic's 1M-context beta header. If any of those models is actually limited to 200k without the header, runs that grow past 200k will fail at the provider instead of being compacted. That limit hasn't been checked for each model.

prs.title: Guard git sync, reimport and Solution deploy against silent data loss
prs.body:
Three narrow data-safety guards for workspace git sync, Maintenance Reimport and Solution deploy. These are interim fixes. A larger redesign of this area is planned separately, so this PR doesn't restructure anything.

## Behaviour changes

| # | Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3 | A full workspace git sync brings in a workflow whose `(path, function_name)` matches a Solution-owned workflow | The Solution row is matched by natural key, re-keyed to the repo id and overwritten. It stays marked as Solution-owned. | The match only considers workspace rows (`solution_id IS NULL`). The workspace entry gets its own row, and the Solution row keeps its id and content. The same scoping now applies to the app, table, policy-rule and claim prefetches. |
| R4a | Workspace sync where the merged repo has no `.bifrost/` manifest, or one that lists no entities, while the DB has workspace entities | The plan deletes every workspace entity. With `confirm_deletes` it applies. | The sync is refused with `WorkspaceSourceMissing`. The error says nothing was changed and asks you to restore the manifest. |
| R4b | Maintenance Reimport when workspace storage (`_repo/`) holds no workspace files | Every file-backed entity (workflows, apps) is deleted, with no confirmation. | Reimport is refused with `WorkspaceSourceMissing`. The platform job fails with code `workspace_source_missing` (not retryable) and shows the message instead of "failed unexpectedly". |
| D | A Solution bundle has an agent that delegates to an agent appearing later in the bundle | The delegation is silently dropped because the child row doesn't exist yet when the parent is indexed. | Parents with forward in-bundle delegations are indexed again once every bundle agent exists, so the delegation is kept. |
| D' | A Solution bundle agent delegates to an agent that is neither in the bundle nor on the instance | The delegation is dropped and only a warning is logged. | The deploy fails with `SolutionDeployConflict`, naming the agent and the missing target. |

**Call-out:** a sync or reimport with an empty or missing manifest now **refuses** instead of offering to delete everything. If you really want to remove every workspace entity, delete them in Bifrost first, then sync. A Solution bundle with a delegation to an agent that doesn't exist now fails deploy where it used to deploy without that delegation.

## Changes

- `api/src/services/manifest_import.py`: `_prefetch_existing_entities` always scopes the workflow, app, table, policy-rule and claim lookups to `solution_id IS NULL`. Before, workflows and apps were scoped only on the partial-import path. I removed the `_workspace_global_scope` flag that gated this. Forms and agents resolve by id only. File-policy keys already include `solution_id`.
- `api/src/services/github_sync.py`: adds `WorkspaceSourceMissing(SyncError)`. `prepare_desktop_sync` refuses when the plan removes entities and the merged manifest is empty. This covers `desktop_sync` and `desktop_connect`. `reimport_from_repo` refuses when storage has no files outside `.git/` and `.bifrost/` and the dry-run deletion plan isn't empty. Both checks run before any DB write. This mirrors the Solutions `NotASolutionWorkspace` guard.
- `api/src/jobs/platform/reimport.py`: maps `WorkspaceSourceMissing` to `PlatformJobFailure("workspace_source_missing", ...)`.
- `api/src/services/solutions/deploy.py`: `_upsert_agents` checks delegation targets up front (`_check_agent_delegations`). It then indexes parents again when they have forward in-bundle delegations.

## Tests added (each red before the fix, green after)

- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestPullUpsertNaturalKeys::test_workspace_sync_leaves_solution_workflow_with_same_path`
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestPullUpsertNaturalKeys::test_workspace_prefetch_excludes_solution_owned_rows`
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestMissingManifestGuard::test_sync_refuses_remote_without_manifest`
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestMissingManifestGuard::test_reimport_refuses_empty_workspace_storage`
- `tests/unit/jobs/test_workspace_reimport_platform_job.py::test_reimport_reports_missing_workspace_source_as_structured_failure`
- `tests/unit/test_solution_form_agent_deploy.py::TestAgentBindingsDeploy::test_delegation_to_a_later_bundle_agent_deploys`
- `tests/unit/test_solution_form_agent_deploy.py::TestAgentBindingsDeploy::test_delegation_to_an_unknown_agent_fails_deploy`

## Verification (run locally on this branch, based on current `origin/main` 593a8818a)

- `./test.sh stack up`
- Red run before the fix, with the new tests: 6 failed and 1 collection error (the reimport job test imports the new exception). The sync, reimport, prefetch and delegation tests failed on the behaviour itself.
- `./test.sh <new tests> tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestPullUpsertNaturalKeys tests/unit/test_solution_form_agent_deploy.py tests/unit/jobs/test_workspace_reimport_platform_job.py`: **35 passed**
- Targeted unit set: **399 passed**. Files: `tests/unit/test_manifest*.py`, `tests/unit/services/test_manifest_jit.py`, `tests/unit/test_solution_git_sync.py`, `tests/unit/test_solution_deploy_{reconcile,s3_after_commit,shells,validation,version}.py`, `tests/unit/test_solution_form_agent_deploy.py`, `tests/unit/test_solution_capture*.py`, `tests/unit/test_solution_zip_install*.py`, `tests/unit/test_workspace_bundle_{hardening,import,memory,plan}.py`, `tests/unit/test_sync_ops.py`, `tests/unit/jobs/test_{workspace_reimport,solution_git_sync,solution_deploy}_platform_job.py`
- Targeted e2e set: **142 passed**. Files: `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py` (whole file), `test_workspace_bundle_{import,kitchen_sink,repo_preview}.py`, `test_workspace_reimport_memory.py`, `test_workspace_reindex.py`, `test_solution_roundtrip.py`, `test_solution_zip_install_e2e.py`, `test_solution_git_connected_e2e.py`, `test_solution_deploy_blank_name.py`, `test_solution_git_sync_events.py`, `tests/e2e/api/test_agent_delegation_lifecycle.py`
- `./test.sh quality api`: pyright 0 errors, ruff all checks passed

I didn't run the full backend unit or e2e suites, client suites or `./test.sh pre-pr`. The merge queue covers the complete suite.

## Known limits of these interim guards

- R4 only covers a source that is completely empty. A manifest that still lists some entities but drops others still goes through the normal delete-confirmation flow, and reimport still deletes file-backed entities whose individual files are missing when storage isn't empty.
- R3 scopes natural-key matching only. A workspace manifest entry whose **id** equals a Solution row's id would still be upserted by id. That needs a row that moved between scopes and kept its id.
