prs.title: Git sync guards: export-matched deletion sweep, non-destructive reimport, stale-tree refusal, token out of .git/config
prs.body:
Follow-up data-safety and security guards for workspace git sync, after #864. These are interim fixes: a larger redesign of this area is planned separately, so each fix is narrow. There's one commit per fix, plus a refusal-message follow-up and three test-only commits.

## Behaviour changes

**Call-outs:**
- **Maintenance → Reimport no longer deletes anything.** It imports, then lists the entities whose files are missing in its result and message. To remove them, run a git sync and confirm the deletions.
- **Commit, Sync and Discard now refuse to run when workspace files changed after the last Fetch.** The message is: "Workspace files changed since this working copy was last fetched, so continuing could overwrite them. Nothing was changed. Run Fetch to pick up the changes, then try again." Anything that changes a file in Bifrost (editor, MCP, CLI) means the next commit or sync needs a Fetch first. The UI already shows this message through its existing error toast, so there is no UI change.

### R1: the deletion sweep removed rows the export never wrote

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| A git sync while the DB has an inactive agent, an independent V2 app (`repo_path` is NULL), an inactive event source, or an inactive subscription | The generator left these rows out of the manifest, so the sweep treated them as "removed from repo". The sync offered to delete them, and deleted them on confirm. | The generator and the sweep share one predicate, `manifest_generator.export_criteria`. The sweep only considers rows the export could have written. Subscriptions are considered only under an exported workspace source. |
| Maintenance → Reimport, where a workflow's or app's files are missing from storage | Deleted with no confirmation. | Kept. The job result carries `pending_deletes`, and the message lists them (up to 5 names) and says to remove them with a confirmed git sync. Empty storage is still refused, as in #864. |

### R5: Solution-owned events leaked into the workspace manifest

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| A Solution install has an event source or subscription | The workspace manifest exported it. Its subscription referenced a Solution workflow the manifest excludes, so `validate_manifest` reported an unknown workflow, preflight failed, and commit was blocked. | Event sources and subscriptions use the same `solution_id IS NULL` scoping as every other kind. The sweep already spared Solution-owned rows, and a test now pins that. |

### R2: commit and sync could lose platform edits

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Fetch, then a file is edited or created in the editor/MCP/CLI, then Commit + Sync (or Discard) | Commit and Sync ran on the stale `/tmp/git`, and Sync/Discard uploaded it with `aws s3 sync --delete`. The edit was reverted and the new file was deleted. The new e2e test reproduces this against SeaweedFS. | Refused with the message above, and storage is untouched. Fetch, then commit/sync, works and includes the edits. |
| An edit that keeps the file's size, then Fetch | `aws s3 sync` skips an S3 object whose size matches an older local copy, so Fetch never picked up the edit and the next commit pushed the old content. Confirmed by the same test with the flag removed. | `sync_down` passes `--exact-timestamps`. |

How it works: each time `/tmp/git` is mirrored down from S3 or published up to it, `GitRepoManager` records a fingerprint of the `_repo/` listing (keys and ETags, excluding `.bifrost/`, which commit regenerates from the DB). It stores the fingerprint in `.git/bifrost-storage-baseline` and clears it before each transfer, so a failed transfer leaves no trusted baseline. For a download it is taken before the transfer, so a write that lands mid-transfer counts as a change. `commit`, `sync` (including publication retries) and `discard` call `ensure_storage_unchanged` first. A pod restart or another replica with no baseline is refused too, which closes the "clone into an empty `/tmp/git`, then `--delete` everything" path.

I chose a refusal over syncing down first (option a) because local unpublished state can't be mirrored over safely. That state includes a merge awaiting delete confirmation, a conflict in progress, and a local commit. Overlaying S3 onto it either reverts remote changes or loses the merge. I didn't use the Redis `repo_dirty` marker because it misses CLI-push writes and deletes, and fetch never clears it.

Follow-up commit: when the refusal fires and the working tree holds work that Fetch would discard, the message names it. Fetch mirrors storage over the whole tree, including `.git/`. The added text is "You have an unfinished merge with conflict resolutions. Fetch discards it, so you'll need to sync and resolve the conflicts again." or "You have N local commit(s) not yet synced. Fetch discards it/them, so you'll need to redo it/them after fetching." "Nothing was changed" stays, and the behaviour is unchanged.

One race remains: an editor write that lands in the moment between a `sync_up` and its fingerprint listing gets folded into the baseline. Editor writes don't take the git lock, and `sync_up --delete` already had that window before this PR.

### R6: the GitHub PAT was stored and leaked

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Any workspace git operation | The remote was `https://x-access-token:<PAT>@github.com/...`. It was written into `.git/config`, mirrored to S3 `_repo/.git/config` and into every retry checkpoint. | The remote URL has no credentials. `GitHubSyncService(token=...)` sends the token to each git command as an `Authorization: Basic` header through `GIT_CONFIG_*` env vars, scoped to `https://github.com/`, with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`. Nothing is persisted. |
| An existing instance whose `.git/config` already holds the token | Kept indefinitely. | `_open_or_init` resets `origin` to the credential-free URL on the next operation, and the next upload heals storage. |
| A clone failure | `SyncError(f"Failed to clone {url}: {e}")` quoted the tokenized URL, and so did GitPython's cmdline. | URLs no longer contain the token. Job results, job failure messages and the connect-preview 422 are also redacted as a backstop. |
| Disconnect | Only deleted the DB config. | First strips credentials from this process's `/tmp/git/.git/config`, S3 `_repo/.git/config` and every checkpoint's `.git/config`, then deletes the config. A `/tmp/git` in another container (the job runner) is rewritten the next time a git operation opens it there. |

Checked against real GitHub: `tests/e2e/api/test_github.py` ran with `GITHUB_TEST_PAT` set. Connect cloned, merged and published with header auth. Afterwards no file under the runner's `/tmp/git` contained a token, and its `origin` URL had no credentials.

### Test-only commits

- **Leaked e2e state.** Running the git-sync files on their own exposed two leaks that the full suite's ordering hides:
  - `test_deactivation_protection` left a `User` row behind, which broke `platform_admin` registration in later modules.
  - `TestPolicyRuleRoundTrip` left policy rules behind.

  Both are now cleaned up.
- **GitHub connect fixture (`github_configured`).** This failed on main whenever `GITHUB_TEST_PAT` was set and any earlier test left a workspace entity: the test branch has no manifest, so #864 refuses with `WorkspaceSourceMissing`. CI runs without the PAT, so it never showed there. The fixture now writes the manifest git sync would export for the current DB into storage before the preview. The connect then declares every entity. Only a file-backed row whose file is missing can still pause it for delete approval, and the fixture now asserts exactly that narrower case. Reproduced first with a deliberately leaked policy rule: the old fixture failed, the new one passes.
- **Real-storage fixture.** The `storage` fixture in `test_git_sync_storage_freshness.py` no longer deletes other tests' `_repo/` contents. It sets them aside, runs on an empty `_repo/`, deletes only what the test created and restores the rest.

## Known pre-existing issues (out of scope)

- Discarding during a merge conflict uploads the conflict-marker files and `MERGE_HEAD` into live `_repo/` (`desktop_discard` → `sync_up`).
- Local-only git state (a commit, a conflict, a resolved merge, a merge awaiting delete confirmation) lives in one container's `/tmp/git` and is never uploaded until a sync succeeds. `workspace.git` must be pinned to one runner before the scheduler goes multi-replica. Today `k8s/scheduler/deployment.yaml` runs one replica.

## Tests

New tests, each confirmed failing before its fix:
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestDeletionSweepMatchesExport::test_sweep_never_removes_rows_the_export_excludes` (R1)
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestReimportNonDestructive::test_reimport_reports_missing_entities_instead_of_deleting` (R1)
- `tests/unit/jobs/test_workspace_reimport_platform_job.py::test_reimport_reports_kept_deletions_in_its_message` (R1)
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py::TestDeletionSweepMatchesExport::test_workspace_export_omits_solution_owned_events` (R5)
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_storage_freshness.py::test_platform_edits_after_fetch_are_never_overwritten` (R2, real SeaweedFS round trip; before the fix: `assert b'first version\n' == b'second, longer version\n'`)
- `tests/unit/services/test_git_repo_manager.py::TestStorageBaseline` (4 tests) and the `--exact-timestamps` assertion (R2)
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_storage_freshness.py::test_token_never_reaches_disk_or_storage` (R6: legacy tokenized config heals; no PAT in the work dir, any `_repo/` object, or a checkpoint)
- `tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_storage_freshness.py::test_disconnect_removes_stored_credentials` (R6)
- `tests/unit/services/test_github_sync.py`: clone error has no token, tokenized remote is rewritten, auth goes through the environment only (R6)
- `tests/unit/test_git_operation_platform_job.py`: tokenless remote URL with a separate token, failures redacted (R6)

- `tests/unit/services/test_git_repo_manager.py::TestRefusalNamesUnsyncedWork` (4 tests, with real local repos: nothing unsynced, 1 local commit, never fetched, real merge conflict). The three warning cases failed without the change.

Commands and results (stack: `./test.sh stack up`):
- `./test.sh quality api`: pyright 0 errors, ruff all checks passed
- `./test.sh tests/unit/services/test_github_sync.py tests/unit/services/test_git_repo_manager.py tests/unit/test_github_connect.py tests/unit/test_git_operation_platform_job.py tests/unit/routers/test_github_sync_retry.py tests/unit/services/test_manifest_jit.py tests/unit/jobs/test_workspace_reimport_platform_job.py tests/unit/test_manifest_generator.py tests/unit/test_manifest_import.py tests/unit/test_manifest.py tests/unit/test_manifest_scope_aware.py tests/unit/test_manifest_diff.py tests/unit/test_manifest_determinism.py tests/unit/test_sync_ops.py tests/unit/test_contract_version.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py`: **343 passed**

prs.title: Preserve external event subscriptions across Solution redeploys
prs.body:
## Problem

`SolutionDeployer._upsert_events` ran `DELETE FROM event_subscriptions WHERE event_source_id = :source` for every Solution-owned event source, then recreated only the subscriptions in the Solution's `.bifrost/events.yaml`. Any subscription an operator added to a Solution-owned source from outside the Solution (for example, a workspace workflow subscribed to a Solution's topic or schedule) was silently deleted on every redeploy, so an instance couldn't keep a durable listener on a Solution's events.

## Change

The existing `event_subscriptions.solution_id` column already marks ownership (NULL means ad-hoc, set means deploy-managed; the API create path leaves it NULL). No migration was needed.

- **deploy.py:** the per-source subscription delete is scoped to `solution_id == sid`, so redeploy fully replaces the managed set only. Each manifest subscription id goes through `_guard_owner`, so a deploy can't overwrite an external row's PK. Schedule/webhook child rows stay full-replace because the source owns them.
- **capture.py:**
  - `bundle_for` exports only managed subscriptions.
  - `_capture_events`, on first capture and on re-capture alike, adopts only unmanaged subscriptions that target the Solution's own workflows/agents. An operator's listener stays external.
- **Deletion summary (`GET /api/solutions/{id}/deletion-summary`):** new `external_event_subscriptions` field. It counts unmanaged subscriptions that a hard-delete cascades away: those on the install's sources, or targeting its workflows/agents. The hard-delete dialog shows a warning line when it's non-zero. Uninstall stays non-destructive.
- **Docs:** `.claude/skills/bifrost-build/references/entities.md` describes deploy/capture ownership and when external listeners are still removed (source dropped from the manifest, hard-delete). The Codex mirror is synced.

## Tests

`api/tests/unit/test_solution_event_subscription_ownership.py` runs under the always-on write guard and covers:
- an external subscription survives redeploy (no duplicate managed row; the schedule child is still a single row)
- a subscription removed from the manifest is deleted
- an updated subscription is updated in place
- deploy refuses an id collision with an external row
- `bundle_for` / re-capture exclude external listeners
- first capture leaves workflow- and agent-targeted external listeners external
- re-capture adopts an agent subscription only when the agent is the Solution's own
- removing a source from the manifest cascades its external listeners

`api/tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_uninstall_lifecycle.py::test_deletion_summary_counts_external_listeners` checks that the summary count matches the rows the hard-delete actually removes.

`client/src/pages/SolutionDetail.test.tsx` covers the dialog warning.

## Summary

> **Merge order:** this PR merges **after** the separate redaction PR, #870, which has now merged. This branch is rebased on it. The admin integration routes are tagged `integrations.read` because #870 already makes them return the `[SECRET]` placeholder.

RBAC R3a step zero. This PR adds the permission vocabulary the identity routes need before they move to the role model, re-tags the access list and operation catalog to use it, and gives the dormant Platform Operator role its user-support seeds.

**No request handler changes.** Every access-list entry keeps the same `current_gate`, `inline_checks`, `inline_effect`, `intended_change` and `operation_id`. No router, core auth, MCP tool or client file is touched. Nothing reads `role_permissions` at request time. The R2c evaluator is still not called by any request.

### What changes

- **Grammar.** A permission is now `<domain>.<read|readwrite|execute>[.all]`, checked by one parser (`parse_permission`). Role-permission validation, workflow-grant validation and `AccessEntry` all use it. `.all` means extended management detail on objects the holder can already reach. It never widens which organizations they reach. There is no implicit hierarchy.
- **New domains:** `users`, `users.lifecycle`, `roleassignments`, `reports`, `secrets`.
  - `organizations` now covers organization records only.
  - `roles` now covers role definitions and their permission sets only.
  - `metrics` no longer covers ROI reporting, which moves to `reports`.
  - The `secrets` description says it is held by the engine execution principal, and by humans only through an explicit assignment. The Platform Admin wildcard never implies it.
- **Privileged set.** `PRIVILEGED_PERMISSIONS` holds the 19 reviewed permissions, plus the wildcard. Two pure helpers sit in `services/authorization/privilege.py`; neither has a runtime caller:
  - `is_privileged_principal`: true if anything the person holds is privileged, at any boundary.
  - `operator_assignable_role`: an Operator may assign or remove only a non-builtin role with no permissions, and only on a user who is not privileged.
  - `AuthorizationContext.held_permissions` unions the base role, every grant at every boundary, and the wildcard for admins.
- **Dormant evaluator.** The Platform Admin wildcard no longer satisfies `secrets.read`; an admin needs an explicit grant. The 19 deferred management reads move to `.read.all`, so the persona matrix's `PENDING_DECISION` exceptions are gone. The matrix now has exactly two listed difference rules, and each has a test proving every matching entry still produces the difference:
  - a provider-org member on an entry with `intended_change`;
  - a Platform Admin on a `secrets.read` entry.
- **New built-in role, Secrets Reader** (fixed id `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000008`; `...0003` and `...0004` stay forbidden). It is an additional role, never a base role, and holds only `secrets.read`. Like the other built-ins it is hidden from role lists and get. Update, delete and every assignment path return 409. It is assigned to nobody. Its description says it grants decryption through the SDK secret paths for local development, and that the Platform Admin wildcard does not include it. When `secrets.read` is enforced in a later release, a one-time migration will assign Secrets Reader to every Platform Admin at that time, so no admin loses SDK secret access at the cutover.
- **Migration `20261001_r3a_operator_perms`.** Its `down_revision` is `20260929_user_base_perm_fix`, the single head on main, and the result is still one head. It adds `users.read`, `users.readwrite`, `roleassignments.read` and `roleassignments.readwrite` to Platform Operator and updates the role's description, which no longer says "read-only". It also seeds Secrets Reader (role row plus `secrets.read`). The frozen copies are inline, and the downgrade restores the Operator rows and removes Secrets Reader.

### Runtime access, before and after

| Persona | Before | After | Why unchanged |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform Admin | Every superuser-gated route, bypass routes, secret-returning SDK/OAuth routes | Same | Gates and inline checks unchanged; the `secrets.read` wildcard exclusion lives only in the dormant evaluator |
| User (regular / external) | Authenticated routes per object checks; User base role rows | Same; User base role seeds unchanged (`USER_BASE_PERMISSIONS` still derives identically) | `.read.all` and the new domains are never derived into the User role |
| Provider-org member (non-admin) | Bypass routes (`engine_or_bypass`, `has_scope_bypass`) | Same | `intended_change` markers unchanged; no bypass change |
| Secrets Reader holder | Role does not exist | Role exists; no one holds it; any assignment returns 409 | role_permissions not read at request time |
| Platform Operator holder | No one holds it | No one holds it; seed rows gain four permissions | Role assigned to nobody; role_permissions not read at request time |
| Custom role holder | Per-entity role grants (forms/apps/workflows/agents) | Same | No handler reads the re-tagged permission strings; validation now also accepts `.all` and new domains |

Evidence: comparing `docs/generated/access-list.json` on `origin/main` with this branch gives 742 entries before and after, the same keys, and 0 differences in `access_class`, `current_gate`, `inline_checks`, `inline_effect`, `intended_change` or `operation_id`. `legacy_oracle.legacy_decide` reads only those fields, so every legacy decision is identical. `git diff origin/main -- api/src/routers api/src/core api/src/services/mcp_server client` is empty.

### Catalog re-tags (76 access-list entries; MCP tools inherit their REST route)

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/users`, `GET /api/users/{id}` | `organizations.read`@platform | `users.read`@organization |
| invite resend/send/regenerate/revoke, `POST /auth/admin/revoke-user` | `organizations.readwrite`@platform | `users.readwrite`@organization |
| `POST /api/users`, `PATCH /api/users/{id}`, `PATCH /api/users/bulk`, `DELETE /api/users/{id}` | `organizations.readwrite`@platform | `users.lifecycle.readwrite`@organization (reason records the field/operation split) |
| `GET /api/users/{id}/roles`, `GET /api/users/{id}/forms` | `roles.read`@platform | `roleassignments.read`@organization |
| `/api/roles/{id}/users*` | `roles.*`@organization | `roleassignments.*`@organization |
| `/api/roles` and `/api/roles/{id}` definition CRUD (+ `bifrost_role_*`) | `roles.*`@organization | `roles.*`@platform |
| `GET /api/roles/{id}/{workflows,apps,forms,agents}` | `roles.read` | `<entity>.read.all`@organization |
| `POST/DELETE /api/roles/{id}/{workflows,apps,forms,agents}*` | `roles.readwrite` | `<entity>.readwrite`@organization |
| `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/organizations*` (+ MCP) | `organizations.*`@platform | `organizations.*`@organization (create stays @platform) |
| `/api/sdk/config/get`, `/api/sdk/integrations/{get,get_mapping,list_mappings,refresh_token}` | `configs.read` / `integrations.read` / `integrations.readwrite` | `secrets.read`@organization |
| `GET /api/oauth/credentials/{name}` | `integrations.read` | `integrations.read` (unchanged permission). After #870 it returns `[SECRET]` instead of the tokens, so it is metadata only |
| 19 deferred management reads | `settings.read` / `apps.read` / `forms.read` / `agentruns.read` / `mcp.read` / `metrics.read` | `apps.read.all`, `forms.read.all`, `agentruns.read.all`, `mcp.read.all`, `workflows.read.all`, `settings.read.all`, `reports.read.all` |
| `POST /api/admin/roi/settings` | `settings.readwrite`@organization | `reports.readwrite`@organization (beside its GET) |
| Catalog `workflows.roles.grant/revoke` | `workflows.readwrite`, `roles.readwrite` | `workflows.readwrite` |

### Seed changes

| Role | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Platform Admin | wildcard in code, no rows | unchanged |
| User | 9 reads | unchanged |
| Platform Operator | 10 reads | + `users.read`, `users.readwrite`, `roleassignments.read`, `roleassignments.readwrite`; never `secrets.read`, `users.lifecycle.readwrite`, `roles.readwrite` or any `.all` |

| Secrets Reader (new, `...0008`) | — | `secrets.read` only; additional (not base), immutable, hidden, assigned to nobody |

### Classification notes and deviations

- **`/api/roles/{id}/{apps,forms,agents}` GET use `.read.all`, not the plain entity read.** The User base role holds `apps.read`, `forms.read` and `agents.read`. Tagging these superuser-gated reads with the plain read would grant them to every member in the dormant evaluator and break the matrix. `workflows` uses `.read.all` too, for consistency.
- **`GET /api/users/{id}/forms` is `roleassignments.read`, not `forms.read`.** It projects a user's role assignments onto form ids, so it reads role assignments. `forms.read` would also reach every member through the User role.
- **`/api/sdk/integrations/list_mappings` is `secrets.read`.** Each mapping's merged config includes decrypted secret values.
- **`/api/sdk/config/list` stays `configs.read`.** It redacts secrets as `[SECRET]`.
- **`get_mapping` returns decrypted secret config, not tokens.** It is `secrets.read` for that reason.
- **Extensions beyond the listed routes:**
  - The catalog's `workflows.roles.grant/revoke` drop `roles.readwrite`; sharing an entity belongs to that entity's domain.
  - `metrics` no longer describes ROI.
  - The legacy runtime helper `role_has_permission` (the agent self-promotion check) still treats the Platform Admin role as satisfying any permission, `secrets.read` included. It is left alone because it is runtime code.
- **Resolved review questions:**
  1. The admin integration routes that return decrypted secret config stay `integrations.read`. These are GET `/api/integrations/{id}`, `.../config`, `.../mappings/{mapping_id}` and `.../mappings/by-org/{org_id}`, plus the PUT config and mapping create/update writes that echo config. Their reasons now record the rule: secret values are redacted for everyone at the cutover, admins included, and only the `secrets.read` decrypt paths return plain text. The `secrets` domain description says the same. No runtime change.
  2. `POST /api/admin/roi/settings` moves to `reports.readwrite`, beside its GET. The `settings` domain no longer lists ROI targets.
- **After rebasing on #870:**
  - The admin integration reasons now describe the `[SECRET]` placeholder those routes already return.
  - `GET /api/oauth/credentials/{name}` is no longer a decrypt path, so it stays `integrations.read` (confirmed in review). It was tagged `secrets.read` in an earlier revision of this PR.
  - Decided in review: `/api/sdk/integrations/upsert_mapping` stays `integrations.readwrite` because it is a write. Its reason now records that the response echoes the decrypted merged config, and that at the R3b cutover the echo is redacted unless the caller holds `secrets.read` (the engine execution principal does).
- **CodeQL `py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data` (7 alerts on the previous head).**
  - Cause: in the PR's SARIF, every data flow starts at the test's `SECRETS_READER_ROLE_ID` (`tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_roles_service.py:501`). From there the role id passes through `update_role`, `delete_role` and `assign_users_to_role` into the role-id log lines in `shared/sdk_roles.py`, `shared/role_cache.py` and `src/core/cache/invalidation.py`. CodeQL's name-based heuristic treats any value held in an identifier containing "secret" as a secret.
  - Fix: the identifiers are renamed `DECRYPTION_ROLE_ID`, `DECRYPTION_ROLE_PERMISSIONS` and `DECRYPT_PERMISSION`. The role name "Secrets Reader" and the permission string `secrets.read` are unchanged, and the logging is unchanged.
  - Local CodeQL 2.25.2 on the rebased head: `CleartextLogging.ql` reports none of the 7. Its 11 remaining results all predate this PR and are dismissed as false positives on main (#127–#137). The full security-and-quality suite reports no error-level results.

## Test plan

Commands (`./test.sh stack up` once, then `./test.sh stack reset` after adding the migration, then rerun after rebasing on current `origin/main`):

- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_permission_vocabulary.py tests/unit/authorization/ tests/unit/test_role_permissions_service.py tests/unit/test_builtin_roles.py tests/unit/test_access_list.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_catalog.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_inventory.py tests/unit/core/test_main_app_operation_id_capture.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py tests/unit/test_contract_version.py tests/unit/test_mcp_thin_wrapper.py tests/unit/test_skill_appendix_fresh.py tests/unit/test_workflow_permissions_service.py tests/unit/test_r2b_roles_migration.py tests/unit/test_external_access_gates.py tests/unit/test_integrations_external.py tests/unit/test_config_merged_external.py tests/unit/test_resolve_scope_sdk.py tests/unit/test_role_cache.py tests/unit/test_user_roles_system_account_constraint.py tests/unit/test_is_superuser_single_writer.py tests/unit/test_migration_tombstones.py` → **390 passed, 0 failed**
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_r3a_operator_perms_migration_rehearsal.py tests/e2e/platform/test_r2b_roles_migration_rehearsal.py tests/e2e/platform/test_builder_residue_migration_rehearsal.py tests/e2e/api/test_users.py tests/e2e/api/test_users_bulk.py tests/e2e/api/test_user_invites.py tests/e2e/api/test_roles.py tests/e2e/api/test_roles_bulk.py tests/e2e/api/test_roles_consumers.py tests/e2e/api/test_organizations.py tests/e2e/api/test_permissions.py tests/e2e/api/test_oauth.py tests/e2e/api/test_config.py tests/e2e/api/test_integrations.py tests/e2e/api/test_org_scoping_scenarios.py tests/e2e/platform/test_sdk_config_local.py tests/e2e/platform/test_sdk_integrations_local.py tests/e2e/platform/test_sdk_integration_mutations_local.py tests/e2e/platform/test_external_users.py tests/e2e/platform/test_cli_roles.py tests/e2e/platform/test_cli_orgs.py tests/e2e/platform/test_cli_configs.py tests/e2e/platform/test_cli_integrations.py` → **263 passed, 0 failed**
- `./test.sh quality api` → pyright 0 errors, ruff all checks passed
- `alembic heads` → one head, `20261001_r3a_operator_perms`
- Regenerated `docs/generated/access-list.json`, `docs/generated/operation-surface-inventory.json` and `operations.md`, then ran `scripts/sync-codex-skills.sh`. The freshness tests pass.

New tests:
- `test_permission_vocabulary.py`: the grammar, the privileged set (valid, every permission used by an entry, pinned), and the wildcard exclusion.
- `authorization/test_privilege.py`: stitched custom roles, privileged at Org B only is still protected at Org A, and the Operator assignment rule.
- `test_evaluator.py::TestSecretDecryption`.
- New matrix rule tests.
- Operator seed rules in `test_builtin_roles.py`.
- `test_r3a_operator_perms_migration_rehearsal.py`: upgrade from the previous revision, idempotent at head, downgrade restores the previous rows.

Follow-up commit (review questions): reran the unit files above, minus the external/scope-gate, migration and role-cache files, which this commit cannot affect. Result: `./test.sh tests/unit/test_permission_vocabulary.py tests/unit/authorization/ tests/unit/test_role_permissions_service.py tests/unit/test_builtin_roles.py tests/unit/test_access_list.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_catalog.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_inventory.py tests/unit/core/test_main_app_operation_id_capture.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py tests/unit/test_contract_version.py tests/unit/test_mcp_thin_wrapper.py tests/unit/test_skill_appendix_fresh.py tests/unit/test_workflow_permissions_service.py` → **337 passed, 0 failed**. `./test.sh quality api` is clean. The access-list JSON was regenerated. The operation inventory, skill appendices and Codex mirrors were unchanged, and their freshness tests pass. The gate fields still match origin/main for all 742 entries.

Follow-up commit (Secrets Reader), on a fresh stack:
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_permission_vocabulary.py tests/unit/authorization/ tests/unit/test_role_permissions_service.py tests/unit/test_builtin_roles.py tests/unit/test_access_list.py tests/unit/sdk/test_sdk_roles_service.py tests/unit/sdk/test_set_user_base_role.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_catalog.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_inventory.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py tests/unit/test_contract_version.py tests/unit/test_mcp_thin_wrapper.py tests/unit/test_skill_appendix_fresh.py tests/unit/test_r2b_roles_migration.py tests/unit/test_migration_tombstones.py tests/unit/test_role_cache.py tests/unit/test_user_roles_system_account_constraint.py tests/unit/test_is_superuser_single_writer.py` → **375 passed, 0 failed**
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/platform/test_r3a_operator_perms_migration_rehearsal.py tests/e2e/platform/test_r2b_roles_migration_rehearsal.py tests/e2e/platform/test_builder_residue_migration_rehearsal.py tests/e2e/platform/test_withdrawn_builder_migrations.py tests/e2e/api/test_roles.py tests/e2e/api/test_roles_bulk.py tests/e2e/api/test_roles_consumers.py tests/e2e/api/test_users.py tests/e2e/api/test_users_bulk.py tests/e2e/platform/test_cli_roles.py` → **53 passed, 0 failed**
- `./test.sh quality api` → clean
- `alembic heads` → one head (`20261001_r3a_operator_perms`)
- The access-list JSON, operation inventory, skill appendices and Codex mirrors are unchanged.

New Secrets Reader coverage:
- Its id is distinct and not one of the forbidden ids.
- It is built-in but not a base role, and `set_user_base_role` rejects it.
- Its frozen literal is pinned to the migration and equals `WILDCARD_EXCLUDED_PERMISSIONS`.
- It is hidden from role list and get; update, delete and user assignment return 409.
- A holder is privileged, and `operator_assignable_role` refuses it.
- The evaluator lets a Platform Admin holding Secrets Reader decrypt at that boundary.
- The rehearsal checks the role row, its permission, zero assignments and its removal on downgrade.
- I did not add it to the persona matrix. The legacy oracle has no way to represent a role nobody can hold today, and the evaluator tests cover the grant.

prs.title: Redact decrypted secrets from admin REST, MCP, and CLI surfaces
prs.body:
## Summary

Plain-text secrets now leave the API only through the `/api/sdk/*` routes the workflow engine uses. Those routes and their gates are unchanged. Every other route that returned a decrypted secret, or echoed stored ciphertext, now returns the existing `[SECRET]` placeholder (`SECRET_PLACEHOLDER` in `src/core/security.py`). Response shapes are unchanged, so a field being present still means a value is set. MCP tools and CLI commands wrap these routes, so they now show the placeholder too. E2E tests cover all three surfaces.

No issue is linked. I couldn't find an existing one for this work and didn't file one without approval.

## Audit inventory: non-SDK paths that decrypt or emit secrets

| # | Path | Gate today | Secret | Internal consumers | Need plaintext? | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /api/integrations/{id}`: `config_defaults` and `mappings[].config` | Superuser | Integration config fields marked secret (default and per-org) | UI `IntegrationOverview.tsx` (presence only, shows dots); `IntegrationDetail.tsx` defaults dialog and `OrgConfigDialog.tsx` (pre-fill, then save back); `ConfigFieldInput.tsx:30` (`Boolean(value)`); CLI `integrations get`; MCP `bifrost_integration_get` | No. The UI round-trip is handled server-side (see below) | **Redacted** |
| 2 | `GET`/`PUT /api/integrations/{id}/config` (PUT echoes) | Superuser | Integration default secret fields | UI save mutation (does not read the echo); no CLI/MCP read of the echo | No | **Redacted** |
| 3 | `POST /api/integrations/{id}/mappings`, `GET …/mappings/{mid}`, `GET …/mappings/by-org/{org}`, `PUT …/mappings/{mid}` | Superuser | Org-override secret fields | UI create/update mapping (cache invalidation only); CLI `add-mapping`/`update-mapping`; MCP `bifrost_integration_mapping_create`/`_update` | No | **Redacted** |
| 4 | `GET /api/oauth/credentials/{connection_name}` | Superuser | OAuth `access_token`, `refresh_token` | `client/src/hooks/useOAuth.ts:305` `useOAuthCredentials`: defined, **never called**. No CLI, MCP, SDK or workflow caller (workflows use `/api/sdk/integrations/*`) | No | **Redacted** (route and metadata kept) |
| 5 | `POST /api/config`, `PUT /api/config/{id}` (echo) | Superuser | Secret config: echoed **Fernet ciphertext** | Router cache write read `result.value` (**needs the stored value**); CLI `configs set/create/update`; MCP `bifrost_config_create/_update`; UI `ConfigDialog` (ignores the echo) | Cache needs ciphertext; callers need neither | **Redacted**. The cache now gets the stored value through `ConfigWrite.stored_value` |
| 6 | `GET /api/config`, `GET /api/config/{id}` | Superuser | Secret config | — | — | Already masked; unchanged |
| 7 | `POST /api/oauth/callback/{name}`, `mcp_connections` client-credentials activate, `mcp_oauth_callback`, `oauth_provider` refresh, `webhooks/auth.py`, `mcp_client/auth_resolution.py` | Various | OAuth client secret, tokens | Decrypted only to call the vendor token endpoint or to authenticate outbound requests; responses carry status only | — | Not emitted; unchanged |
| 8 | `embed.py` (`GET /embed/apps/{slug}`, `GET /embed/forms/{form_id}`) | HMAC | App/form embed secrets | Decrypted only to verify the HMAC; responses carry a session JWT | — | Not emitted; unchanged |
| 9 | `export_import.py` config/integration export | Superuser | Secret config, OAuth client secret | Exported as **instance ciphertext** (`contains_encrypted_values`); import re-encrypts using `source_secret_key` | — | Encrypted export by design; unchanged |
| 10 | Solution full-backup export (`capture._config_values` → `secrets_blob`) | Superuser | Secret config plaintext | Only written into the password-encrypted (scrypt + Fernet) `.bifrost/secrets.enc` | — | Encrypted export by design; unchanged |
| 11 | Platform-job `encrypted_payload`, solution export `encrypted_options` | Internal | Workspace import config values, export password | Decrypted only inside the runner/scheduler; `PlatformJobPublic` carries no payload | — | Not emitted; unchanged |
| 12 | `oauth_connections` detail/list, `integrations/{id}/oauth`, SSO `oauth_config`, `llm_config`/`ai_models`, `github` config, `mcp_connections`/`mcp_servers` | Superuser | Client secrets, API keys, GitHub token | Responses carry only `*_set` / `token_saved` flags; `*Public` models omit secrets | — | Already safe; unchanged |
| 13 | `src/services/oauth_storage.py::get_tokens` | — | OAuth tokens | No callers anywhere | — | Unreachable; unchanged |
| 14 | Logs, WebSocket payloads | — | — | Searched for token/secret values in log calls and pubsub; only presence flags are logged | — | None found |

### Unchanged SDK paths (per the product rule)

`/api/sdk/config/get|set|list`, `/api/sdk/integrations/get|list_mappings|get_mapping|upsert_mapping|refresh_token` are unchanged. Note that `upsert_mapping` echoes the merged, decrypted config. It is an SDK route, so it is left for the later permission change.

## Before / after per surface

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/integrations/{id}` `config_defaults.api_key` | plaintext | `[SECRET]` |
| `GET /api/integrations/{id}` `mappings[].config.api_key` | plaintext | `[SECRET]` |
| `GET`/`PUT /api/integrations/{id}/config` `config.api_key` | plaintext | `[SECRET]` |
| Mapping create/get/by-org/update `config.api_key` | plaintext | `[SECRET]` |
| `PUT …/config` or `PUT …/mappings/{mid}` with `api_key: "[SECRET]"` | would store the literal string | keeps the stored secret (no-op for that key) |
| `GET /api/oauth/credentials/{name}` `credentials.access_token` / `refresh_token` | plaintext | `[SECRET]` / `[SECRET]` (`null` when no refresh token); status, `expires_at`, `scopes` and `integration_id` unchanged. A decrypt failure no longer returns 500, because nothing is decrypted |
| `POST`/`PUT /api/config` `value` for a secret | Fernet ciphertext | `[SECRET]` (cache still receives the ciphertext) |
| CLI `bifrost integrations get`, `bifrost configs set/create/update` | as REST | `[SECRET]` |
| MCP `bifrost_integration_get`, `_mapping_create/_update`, `bifrost_config_create/_update` | as REST | `[SECRET]` |

## Internal consumers checked

- **Integration admin UI.** `OrgConfigDialog.tsx` and the defaults dialog in `IntegrationDetail.tsx` pre-fill the form from the read and send every non-empty value back on save. If nothing changed on the server, the redacted placeholder would have overwritten the real secret. `_save_config` in the router now skips a secret-typed key whose value is exactly `[SECRET]`. No client change is needed. `ConfigFieldInput.tsx:30` and `IntegrationOverview.tsx` only check presence. The `ConfigDialog` config page already omits unchanged secrets.
- **Config cache.** `routers/config.py` wrote `result.value` (ciphertext) into Redis. On global writes this is `HSET` into the shared hash that the SDK decrypts. The repository now returns `ConfigWrite(response, stored_value)`, and the router caches `stored_value`. Mutation check: caching the masked response instead makes `test_secret_write_echoes_are_redacted` fail.
- **SDK / engine.** `shared/sdk_integrations.py` uses `src.repositories.integrations.IntegrationsRepository`, not the router-local class I changed. prs.title: Make webhook signing secrets reveal-once and encrypted at rest
prs.body:
## Summary

A generic webhook source's HMAC signing secret was stored in plaintext twice: in `webhook_sources.config["secret"]` and in `webhook_sources.state["secret"]`. Every event-source read returned it, through REST, MCP, CLI and the edit dialog, which pre-filled it into a password input. Git-sync manifests and Solution bundles also carried it.

The secret is now **reveal-once and write-only**:

- It is stored only as Fernet ciphertext (`encrypt_secret`), in `state["secret_encrypted"]`. It is never in `config`.
- Only the generic adapter decrypts it, when it verifies an incoming request.
- The create response and the new rotate endpoint return the plaintext once, in a dedicated `raw_secret` field.
- Every other surface shows only `webhook.secret_set: bool`.

No issue is linked. I didn't find an existing one and didn't file one without approval.

## Before / after by surface

| Surface | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DB `webhook_sources.config` | plaintext `secret` | no `secret` key |
| DB `webhook_sources.state` | plaintext `secret` | `secret_encrypted` (Fernet ciphertext) |
| `POST /api/events/sources` response | secret in `webhook.config` | `raw_secret` (shown once), `webhook.secret_set` |
| `GET /api/events/sources`, `GET /api/events/sources/{id}` | secret in `webhook.config` | `webhook.secret_set` only |
| `PATCH /api/events/sources/{id}` response | secret in `webhook.config` | `webhook.secret_set` only |
| `POST /api/events/sources/{id}/rotate-secret` | did not exist | **new**: returns the new secret once in `raw_secret` |
| MCP `bifrost_event_source_get` / `_list` / `_update` | secret in payload | `secret_set` only (thin wrappers over REST) |
| MCP `bifrost_event_source_create` | secret in payload | `raw_secret` passes through from REST (the caller supplied it) |
| CLI `events get-source` / `list-sources` / `update-source` | secret in output | `secret_set` only |
| CLI `events create-source` | secret in output | `raw_secret` once |
| CLI `events rotate-secret <ref>` | did not exist | **new**: generates a secret and prints `raw_secret` once |
| `.bifrost/events.yaml` (git sync), Solution capture/bundles | carried `webhook_config.secret` | never carried; on import, a legacy manifest's `secret` is dropped |
| Solution redeploy | wiped `state` every deploy | keeps the stored encrypted secret |
| Provider resubscribe (`/resubscribe`, adapter/config change on PATCH) | generic secret survived only because it was re-copied from `config` | encrypted secret carried explicitly |
| UI edit dialog | plaintext pre-filled into a password input | blank write-only input, a "Secret configured" badge, and "Leave blank to keep the current secret" |
| UI detail page | — | "Rotate signing secret" action with a one-time reveal (`HmacSecretReveal`) |
| Logs / audit | not logged | not logged; the rotate audit event records only `generated: bool` |

## Behaviour changes

- **Reveal once.** `POST /api/events/sources` returns `EventSourceSecretResponse`, which is `EventSourceResponse` plus `raw_secret`. `raw_secret` holds the secret supplied as `webhook.config.secret`, or `null` when none was set. No later call returns it.
- **Rotate flow.** `POST /api/events/sources/{id}/rotate-secret` takes `{"secret": "<value>"}` (caller-supplied, `min_length=1`) or `{}` (server-generated with `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`).
  - It returns the new secret once in `raw_secret`.
  - Requests signed with the old secret are rejected immediately (401).
  - It returns 400 for sources whose adapter doesn't declare a signing secret (schedule, topic, Graph, and so on).
  - It is allowed on Solution-managed sources. No bundle carries the secret and redeploys keep it, so this is now the only way to set a secret on a Solution-installed webhook.
  - Audit event: `event_source.rotate_secret`.
  - The rotate route mirrors the existing `resubscribe` route: REST + CLI + UI, with no operation-catalog entry and no MCP tool. It is listed in `access_list.py` as `events.readwrite`, superuser-gated.
- **PATCH `webhook.config.secret` is write-only.** Leaving the key out keeps the stored secret. A non-empty value replaces it. `null` or `""` clears it. The old behaviour was different: any config change re-subscribed and rebuilt `state` from `config`, so a PATCH without the secret silently removed it.
- **Validation.**
  - A non-string `secret` returns 422.
  - A `secret` sent to an adapter that doesn't verify one (e.g. Microsoft Graph) returns 422. Before, it was stored in plaintext config and ignored.
- **Why not `SECRET_PLACEHOLDER` (#870).** That placeholder masks a value that stays in its field. Here the secret is removed from `config` entirely: an adapter config that echoed `"secret": "[SECRET]"` back on save would overwrite the real secret with the placeholder. A separate `secret_set` flag, combined with "a missing key keeps the stored secret", avoids that round-trip hazard. The embed and MCP-connection secrets already use this `*_set` pattern.
- **Manifests.** `ManifestEventSource.webhook_config` drops `secret` in a validator. That covers git-sync export and import, Solution capture, deploy, and the workspace bundle plan. Old manifests that still contain the plaintext parse fine, and the value is discarded.
- **Solution deploy** now reads `webhook_config` from the validated model instead of the raw dict. When it replaces the `WebhookSource` row, it uses `DELETE … RETURNING state` so the encrypted secret moves to the new row.

## Migration notes

`api/alembic/versions/20261001_webhook_secret_encrypt.py` adds revision `20261001_webhook_secret_enc`, with `down_revision = 20261001_r3a_operator_perms` (from #869, which is now merged). After this PR, `alembic heads` shows a single head: `20261001_webhook_secret_enc`.

- **Forward-only data migration.** For every row with a plaintext `secret` in config or state, it encrypts `state.secret` into `state.secret_encrypted` and removes `secret` from both. Each source keeps verifying with exactly the secret it verifies with today.
- **Config-only secrets are dropped, not enforced.** Verification has always read `state`, and Solution deploy and git-sync inserts wrote `config` without `state`. So Solution-installed and freshly git-sync-imported generic webhooks never enforced the `config.secret` they carried. Switching enforcement on during a migration could start 401-ing live senders, so the migration preserves today's behaviour. Operators can set the secret with `rotate-secret`. Reviewers: this is a real latent gap on those installs (they accept unsigned requests today). It is now visible through `secret_set: false` and fixable through rotate.
- **Idempotent.** Rows without a plaintext secret are untouched, and the rehearsal re-runs the data step and asserts nothing changes.
- `downgrade()` is a no-op, because restoring plaintext would undo the change.
- The migration uses the live `src.core.security.encrypt_secret` (as `20260219_backfill_config_types` does), so the adapter can decrypt what it writes.
- **#869 has merged.** This branch is rebased on it, and the migration now follows #869's `20261001_r3a_operator_perms` to keep a single head. A later PR that adds a migration must point at `20261001_webhook_secret_enc`.

## Client changes

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `client/src/lib/v1.d.ts` | Regenerated from this branch's API: `secret_set`, `EventSourceSecretResponse`, `WebhookSecretRotate`, rotate route |
| `client/src/services/events.ts` | `useRotateWebhookSecret` hook; shared source-query invalidation with resubscribe |
| `client/src/services/events.test.ts` | Covers the rotate hook wiring and invalidation |
| `client/src/components/events/DynamicConfigForm.tsx` | `secretConfigured` prop: password fields show a "Secret configured" badge and a keep-if-blank placeholder |
| `client/src/components/events/DynamicConfigForm.test.tsx` | Badge and placeholder; blank keeps, typing replaces |
| `client/src/components/events/EditEventSourceDialog.tsx` | Passes `source.webhook.secret_set` to the config form |
| `client/src/components/events/EditEventSourceDialog.test.tsx` | Saving with a blank secret sends no `secret` key; adds `secret_set` to fixtures |
| `client/src/components/events/EventSourceActions.tsx` | Optional "Rotate signing secret" menu item |
| `client/src/components/events/EventSourceDetail.tsx` | Rotate confirmation dialog with a one-time `HmacSecretReveal`; calls `mutation.reset()` so the secret isn't kept in the mutation cache |
| `client/src/components/events/EventSourceDetail.test.tsx` | Rotate flow, reveal, dismiss; no action for non-generic adapters |
| `client/src/components/forms/HmacSecretReveal.tsx` | Optional `label` prop (defaults to the existing "New embed secret") |
| `client/e2e/event-source-management-acceptance.admin.spec.ts` | Happy path rotates in the UI, reads the reveal, and asserts the API read omits it and reports `secret_set` |

## Tests and commands

Focused local verification against this worktree's test stack. The PR was first rebased on `origin/main` d92e468a7 (#870), then rebased again on f0eaa3486 (#869):

- `./test.sh unit`: 7779 passed, 2 failed before the fixes below. Both failures were expected consequences of this change, not unrelated:

  - Both were fixed in this PR and re-run green.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_contract_version.py tests/unit/test_access_list.py tests/unit/test_skill_appendix_fresh.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_inventory.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_catalog.py tests/unit/test_dto_flags.py tests/unit/test_mcp_thin_wrapper.py tests/unit/services/test_webhook_signing_secret.py tests/unit/services/test_webhook_adapters.py tests/unit/routers/test_events_webhook_secret.py tests/unit/routers/test_events_resubscribe_on_change.py tests/unit/routers/test_events_webhook_creation.py tests/unit/services/test_webhook_lifecycle.py tests/unit/test_manifest.py tests/unit/test_solution_capture.py tests/unit/test_manifest_codec.py tests/unit/jobs/test_webhook_renewal.py`: **456 passed**.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_events.py tests/e2e/api/test_webhook_signing_secret.py tests/e2e/api/test_webhook_rate_limit.py tests/e2e/api/test_builtin_events.py tests/e2e/platform/test_cli_events.py tests/e2e/mcp/test_mcp_parity.py::TestMcpParityEvents tests/e2e/platform/test_webhook_secret_migration_rehearsal.py tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_event_sub_remap.py tests/e2e/platform/test_solution_readonly_full.py tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_local.py tests/e2e/platform/test_sdk_events_local.py tests/e2e/roundtrip/test_roundtrip_repo.py tests/e2e/roundtrip/test_roundtrip_solution.py tests/e2e/platform/test_watch_regression_disappearing_entity.py`: **222 passed** before the rebase.

prs.title: Unified file index + paged source search (workspace and Solutions)
prs.body:
Fixes #872

## What changed
- **One indexer.** `FileIndexService` is the only code that writes `file_index` (workspace `_repo/`) or the new `solution_file_index` (Solution install source). A guard test enforces this. One policy applies: every tracked object gets a row, with `content` set to the UTF-8 text when it decodes and is ≤ 8 MiB, otherwise NULL (path-only).
  - All writers now go through it: editor/CLI writes, moves and deletes; folder markers; the workflow ref rewriter; app auto-migration; `requirements.txt` saves; git-sync bulk refresh; git desktop discard; presigned-upload completion; Solution deploy.
  - The unreachable `WorkspaceReindexService` is removed.
- **A real reconciler.** The daily/startup job compares hashes, refreshes stale rows and removes orphaned rows across the workspace and every Solution. It never writes to storage (the old one resurrected deleted files). Per-object failures are counted and skipped, commits are batched, and a write only applies while the row still has the hash the reconciler read, so a concurrent save always wins.
- **One search.** `POST /api/files/search` → `src/services/source_search`.
  - By default it covers workspace and all Solution source; `source` / `solution_id` narrow it. Solution hits are labelled read-only.
  - Literal queries are prefiltered in SQL. Each scope is paged by its own primary key, so Postgres walks the index and stops after a page.
  - Globs are ripgrep-style and correct.
  - Pages default to 25 (max 200). The keyset cursor is bound to the query and filters. Each response carries `has_more_matches` / `response_complete` / `next_cursor` plus a `guidance` sentence naming the next call. `output_mode=files` returns one entry per file. Long lines are windowed, and matching is lazy and bounded.
- **Clients.**
  - SDK `files.search(limit, cursor, source, solution_id, output_mode, context_lines)`.
  - CLI: grep-style output with a copy-paste `More results: bifrost files search … --cursor X` line.
  - MCP `bifrost_file_search`: a thin REST wrapper replacing the divergent `search_content`.
  - Editor: "Load more" and read-only Solution badges. Quick Access uses files mode.
- **Migration** `20261001_unified_file_search`:
  - adds `solution_file_index`;
  - `CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm` plus GIN indexes, inside a savepoint. If the extension can't be created, it warns and skips, and search results stay identical, only slower.
  - renames `search_content` → `bifrost_file_search` in `agents.system_tools`.

## Behavior changes to note
- MCP search now inherits the REST route's superuser gate. Provider-org members who aren't platform admins lose MCP search now, rather than at the R3 cutover the old access entry scheduled.
- `.json`, `.ps1`, extensionless and other UTF-8 files are now searchable and listed. The `.json` exclusion only existed for the retired `app.json` format.
- Exclusion globs (`!pattern`) are rejected with a 400 instead of silently matching nothing.

## Verification
- `./test.sh quality api`: 0 errors. `client`: `npm run tsc` clean; `npm run lint` shows 0 errors, and its 5 warnings are in untouched files.
- Focused backend suite (unit + e2e for index, writers, reconciler, globs, search, CLI/SDK/MCP contracts, git sync, scheduler fixtures, skills, authorization, migration rehearsal): **1020 passed**.
- Client: `SearchPanel` / `QuickAccess` vitest (16 passed). Playwright `e2e/editor-search.admin.spec.ts` passed.
- Migration: applied on a fresh test DB. The skip branch was proven with a real non-CREATE role (warning logged, transaction committed, tool renamed, no index). Single Alembic head after merging main.
- **Live drive.** I seeded a debug stack with this repo's 4,355 files via `bifrost push` and five real Solutions via `bifrost solution deploy`, then paged every query to completion with the branch CLI and compared against ripgrep:
  - **8 / 8 exact:** literal, `--include *.py` (24,816 matches across 2,315 files and 125 pages), brace glob, directory glob, regex, case-sensitive, Solution-only.
  - Common-term pages ~0.2–0.5 s.
  - The reconciler at full scale found every row in sync. It added 43 MiB of peak memory and took ~100 s, because it reads each object sequentially.
  - MCP was exercised in-process through the REST bridge.
- Not run: the full `./test.sh all`, the full vitest suite, and the full Playwright suite (left to the merge queue).

## Known limitations / follow-ups
- Regex searches have no SQL prefilter and take ~2–3 s on 4k files. Postgres's regex dialect differs from Python's (e.g. `\b`), so it can't safely prefilter.
- The reconciler downloads every object on each run. Storing ETags would avoid that.
- Solution app TSX isn't searchable: deploys keep it only as a zip.
- In the editor, Solution hits can't be opened (there's no read endpoint for Solution source).

prs.title: Encrypt Microsoft Graph clientState and keep it out of delivered events
prs.body:
## Summary

Microsoft Graph webhook sources register a server-generated `clientState` with Graph. Graph echoes it on every notification, and we compare it to prove the notification is genuine. It is a shared secret, but:

- it was stored in plaintext in `webhook_sources.state["client_state"]`, and
- it was copied into every delivered event payload: the top-level `client_state` field, plus `clientState` on every item in `notifications`. Event history and workflow input therefore carried it.

This follows the pattern from #871 (generic webhook signing secrets):

- `subscribe` stores only Fernet ciphertext (`encrypt_secret`) in `state["client_state_encrypted"]`.
- `handle_request` decrypts it only to validate, using a constant-time compare. A missing or non-string `clientState` on any notification in a batch is rejected with 401.
- `clientState` is removed from every delivered notification. The `client_state` payload field is gone.
- Migration `20261001_graph_client_state_enc` encrypts any existing plaintext `state.client_state` in place and drops the plaintext key, so live subscriptions keep validating without a resubscribe. It is idempotent, and downgrade is a no-op.

## Consumers

- Nothing in the repo (src, tests, docs, skills, client) reads `client_state` / `clientState` from an event payload.
- A grep of the production workspace copy found no workflow consumer either.
- Webhook `state` is never returned by REST/MCP/CLI and is not carried in manifests or Solution bundles.
- Renewal merges state, so it keeps the encrypted value. Recreate and resubscribe generate a fresh value and store it encrypted.

## Revert behavior

- E2E: `tests/e2e/platform/test_graph_client_state_migration_rehearsal.py`, a pre-head rehearsal in #871's style.

prs.title: Refuse git Discard while a merge is in progress
prs.body:
## Summary

Discard publishes the working tree to S3 `_repo/` (`sync_up`) and refreshes the Redis module cache from it. During an unfinished merge, that publishes:

- the conflict markers of files the user did **not** discard,
- `.git/MERGE_HEAD`, `MERGE_MSG`, `MERGE_MODE`, `AUTO_MERGE`, and the conflicted index.

Workers and the editor then read `<<<<<<<`-marked modules from storage and the module cache. A later Fetch pulls the half-finished merge back down.

The UI already disables Discard while conflicts exist (`SourceChangesSection.tsx`), but the API accepted it.

`desktop_discard` now refuses while a merge is in progress (MERGE_HEAD present, or unmerged index entries left by a stash pop). It returns `success=False` with "A merge is in progress. Resolve the conflicts or abort the merge before discarding changes. Nothing was changed." It checks after the existing staleness check and before touching anything. The check is a shared helper `merge_in_progress()`, also used by Fetch's unsynced-work warning.

## Other operations checked

- **Sync mid-merge:** never reaches `sync_up`; it raises `WorkspaceMergeConflict` first.
- **Other `sync_up` callers** (fetch/connect/preflight/reimport checkout exit, post-merge publish): none publish a mid-merge tree.
- **Commit mid-merge:** related but separate. The backend stages with `git add -A`, so an API caller could commit unresolved markers locally. The UI disables Commit while conflicts exist, so no change here. Noted as a follow-up.

No UI changes.

## Tests

`tests/e2e/platform/test_git_sync_storage_freshness.py`:
- `test_discard_during_merge_never_publishes_conflicts` builds a real conflicting merge against a local bare repo and real object storage. It failed before the fix (markers reached storage and the module cache) and passes now.
- `test_discard_after_aborting_merge_publishes_the_revert` checks Discard still works after aborting the merge.

Ran: `test_git_sync_storage_freshness.py`, `test_git_sync_local.py`, `tests/unit/services/test_git_repo_manager.py` (141 passed), the agent's wider git-sync set (157 passed), and `./test.sh quality api` (clean).

prs.title: Keep the shared e2e client anonymous
prs.body:
## Summary

Backend e2e tests share one session-scoped HTTP client (`e2e_client`). Auth fixtures logged users in through it. The server answers login, MFA, and refresh with auth cookies, and it accepts those cookies in place of an `Authorization` header. So the shared cookie jar kept whoever logged in last, and a request meant to be anonymous could silently run as an admin. Results depended on test order, which changes whenever size-based CI shards reshuffle. This is the cause of the 200-instead-of-403 queue failure on #867, which was patched there with a one-off `cookies.clear()`.

Now:

- `_register_and_authenticate_user` / `_login_user` in `tests/e2e/fixtures/setup.py` do credential exchanges on a throwaway private client. They no longer take a client argument; call sites are updated.
- New `private_client` fixture (own cookie jar) for tests that deliberately exercise login, MFA, refresh, or logout. It's used by six `test_auth.py` tests and the device-flow refresh test.
- New autouse `shared_client_has_no_ambient_auth` fails any test that leaves cookies in the shared client, then clears the jar. On its first run it caught three tests that logged in through the shared client (`test_mfa_login_with_totp`, `test_refresh_token_rejected_as_access_token`, `test_refresh_token_rotation`); they now use `private_client`.
- `test_client_isolation.py` asserts the jar is empty after the admin/org-user fixtures and token refresh, and that an unauthenticated request gets 401.

prs.title: RBAC R3a: identity routes on the authorization evaluator + role configuration UI
prs.body:
## Summary

RBAC R3a: users, organizations, roles and role assignments now decide access with the role and permission model through the authorization evaluator, and the UI follows what the signed-in person can actually do.

**Live access change at merge: none for existing accounts.** Nobody holds Platform Operator or any identity permission today. Platform Admins keep everything. Users, External users, provider-organization members and workflow engine tokens get the same decisions as before. Engine and service tokens keep their current decision on identity routes until R3b gives them a typed principal.

### What's in it
- **Backend:** the identity routes are decided by `src.services.authorization.enforce` at the target's organization. A user holding any privileged permission is *protected*: only a Platform Admin may change them. Non-admins can grant only roles with no permissions. Every role assignment now records its boundary, and a backfill migration adds home-organization boundaries to existing assignments. 42 of 748 access-catalog entries are on the evaluator.
- **New endpoints:** `GET /auth/authorization` (the caller's effective grants), `GET|PUT /api/users/{id}/role-assignments`, `GET|PUT /api/roles/{id}/permissions` (identity permissions only), and `POST /api/users/{id}/mfa/reset`.
- **Platform Admin is an additional role, not a base role.** Every user's base role is User or a custom role (a custom base can lower permissions further). Platform Admin is held as an additional role that applies everywhere; only a Platform Admin can grant or remove it, and only to provider-organization or Global users. A migration moves today's admins to base User plus a Platform Admin assignment; `is_superuser` is unchanged for everyone.
- **Permissions resolve from one effective list.** A person's grants are (permission, boundary) pairs: the base role at their home organization plus each additional role at its boundaries. Platform Admin's wildcard (`*`) is stored as its role permission like any other; "is Platform Admin" means holding `*` at the platform boundary. No custom role can be given `*`, and `*` still excludes `secrets.read`. A structural test keeps role-identity checks out of permission resolution.
- **Platform Operator is for provider-organization people only.** It can't be given to anyone outside the provider organization, and a user who holds it can't be moved out of the provider organization; remove Operator first. This applies to single and bulk moves.
- **Reset MFA** removes the user's authenticator app, recovery codes, passkeys and remembered devices, and signs them out everywhere. They enroll again at their next password sign-in. It is audited (`user.mfa_reset`, counts only). It refuses with 409 a user who has no password and no linked SSO account but has a passkey, because they would be left with no way to sign in. You can't reset your own account here; use Security settings.
- **UI:** a Roles & access section in the user dialog; role detail pages show built-in roles and edit identity permissions; a People tab on the Platform Operator and Secrets Reader pages; organization and user actions gated by permission. The users row menu gains Reset MFA and Sign out of all devices.
- **Migrations:** `20261001_r3a_boundary_fill` → `20261001_r3a_operator_desc` → `20261002_r3a_admin_additional` (after `20261001_unified_file_search`), each with a rehearsal test. Single head checked against current main.

### Who can do what after this PR

| Action | Rule after this PR | Platform Operator (customer orgs) |
|---|---|---|
| List and view users | `users.read` where the user belongs; lists filtered | yes |
| Invite an ordinary user | `users.readwrite` in that organization | yes (new: was admin-only) |
| Change name, enable or disable, reset MFA, resend or revoke an invite, sign out of all devices | `users.readwrite`; protected accounts admin-only | yes |
| Move, delete, change email or base role | `users.lifecycle.readwrite`; Platform Admin changes admin-only | no |
| Assign additional roles | `roleassignments.readwrite`; non-admins only roles with no permissions, never on protected accounts | permission-free roles only |
| View organizations | `organizations.read`; filtered | customer orgs |
| Create, edit, disable organizations | `organizations.readwrite` | no |
| Create or edit roles and their permissions | `roles.readwrite` platform-wide | no |

Stricter than before, by design: a demoted admin loses identity access immediately instead of at token expiry. Bulk role replacement never adds built-in roles and leaves built-in roles a user already holds (Platform Admin, Platform Operator) as they are; it manages custom roles only.

**Known limits:** bulk "Replace roles" needs role-list access, so Operators assign roles per user. Moving a user to another organization leaves their additional-role placements where they were (same as today). Secrets Reader stays unassignable until R3b. `PATCH /api/users/{id}` with `mfa_enabled=false` still exists as a flag flip; the UI uses the real reset.

## Test plan

Run locally against this worktree's test stack, after merging current main:
- [x] Full backend unit suite: 8080 passed (after merging main through #882)
- [x] Full client unit suite: 536 files, 3349 tests passed
- [x] `./test.sh quality api`: pyright 0 errors, ruff clean
- [x] Backend unit (425 passed): `test_access_list`, `test_alembic_single_head`, `test_builtin_roles`, `test_contract_version`, `test_dto_flags`, `test_identity_authorization`, `test_mcp_thin_wrapper`, `test_user_mfa_reset`, `tests/unit/authorization/` (incl. `test_decision_matrix`), `services/test_operation_catalog`, `sdk/test_sdk_users_service`, `sdk/test_set_user_base_role`, `test_is_superuser_single_writer`, `test_datetime_consistency`
- [x] Backend e2e (125 passed on the final head, incl. every migration rehearsal; 136 on the earlier head): `api/test_auth`, `test_organizations`, `test_roles*`, `test_users*`, `platform/test_r3a_identity_authorization`, the three R3a migration rehearsals, `test_authorization_deny_probe`, `test_external_users`, `test_cli_roles`, `test_cli_orgs`
- [x] `test_skill_appendix_fresh`, `test_cli_surface_smoke`
- [x] Client: `npm run tsc` clean; `npm run lint` 0 errors (5 warnings in untouched files); vitest 185 passed across the 19 changed test files
- [x] Playwright: `e2e/role-assignments.admin.spec.ts`, `e2e/users-security-actions.admin.spec.ts` (4 passed, incl. granting and removing Platform Admin)
- [x] Driven on a debug stack as a Platform Operator: role assignment, user support actions, MFA reset of a TOTP-enrolled user (old refresh token refused afterwards)

`test_authorization_deny_probe` was failing on this branch: the identity routes now decide permissions after FastAPI validates the body, so the probe's empty body got 422. It now sends a minimal valid body for those 10 routes, and they are refused with 403.

Fixed after the first CI runs:
- `api-client.ts` no longer imports the shared query client (that import broke suites that fully mock `@tanstack/react-query`); `main.tsx` registers the refetch-authorization-on-403 listener instead.

- Two CodeQL unused-import findings were quoted annotations hiding a real use; unquoted.

## Summary

Test-only. Adds `api/tests/e2e/scenarios/`, one e2e module that records how workflow runs are identified and which orgs they act in, for every way a run starts. It is the baseline later RBAC slices (Operator, record-only "started by", R3b managed identities) are checked against. No product code changes.

- **World** (module-scoped): Contoso/Fabrikam/provider personas plus HR (permission-free role), external and custom-base-role users; one observation table per partition; an integration with a mapping per org; global config with a Contoso override and a secret.
- **Probe workflow** in four homes (provider, Contoso, global, new global). One run tries every scope knob (`set_scope`, `tables.insert/upsert/query` with `scope=`, `config.get`, `integrations.get`, raw `bifrost.api`, the context's scope set directly) against Contoso, Fabrikam, provider and global, and can spawn children (depth 2, `run_as`).

- **Checks**: write effects are read back from the tables as admin, not taken from the probe's own report. Each start's cells are compared with the managed-identity model in `rule.py`, except cells listed in `pre_r3b.py` ("pre-MI behaviour (R3b)"), which record today's value. `test_pre_r3b_entries_are_live` fails once an entry matches the model, so the table can only shrink. Separate invariant tests (customers stay in their org, unattended Contoso workflows stay in Contoso, refused writes leave no row, children stay within the starter's reach) are computed straight from the observations.

They hold today and must hold unchanged after R3b.

## Cost

Starting with the authoring rules for expensive e2e tests: there are about 42 worker executions, all launched together and then polled together. prs.body:
## Summary

This is the follow-up to #879. Platform Operator becomes the role provider-organization staff use to support customer organizations, and Platform Admins receive Secrets Reader before R3b starts enforcing it.

- **Platform Operator gains `workflows.execute`**, so staff can run workflows (onboarding, for example) in customer organizations once R3b enforces execution. Its description says so.
- **A migration (`20261003_r3_operator_secrets`) assigns Platform Operator** at "all customer organizations" to every existing provider-organization member who is not a Platform Admin, a system account or an external user (inactive members included). Assignments that already exist keep their own boundaries. New users get nothing automatically.
- **The same migration assigns Secrets Reader** to every Platform Admin who is not a system account, at platform + all customer organizations + the provider organization. It has no effect until `secrets.read` is enforced. A Platform Admin can now assign or remove Secrets Reader, with those fixed boundaries and no picker.
- **`/auth/authorization` returns a Platform Admin's own grants** (`*` at platform, plus Secrets Reader), so Roles & access shows them.
- The downgrade removes only the rows this migration created.

## Before / after

**Provider-organization staff who exist at migration time.** Membership in the provider organization alone grants nothing on the routes already decided by the authorization evaluator, so these routes return 403 for staff today.

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Users list/detail | 403 | Customer-organization users (provider org and Global still 403) |
| Invite/create, invite resend/regenerate/revoke, MFA reset, session revoke, (de)activate | 403 | Ordinary (non-protected) users in customer organizations |
| Organizations list/detail | 403 | Customer organizations readable; create/update/delete and the provider org still 403 |

| Sidebar | No Organizations / Users | Both visible |
| Protected account | No | Yes (only Platform Admins can act on them) |
| Moving them out of the provider org | Allowed | 409 until Platform Operator is removed (existing Operator rule) |
| `workflows.execute` | — | Held; not yet enforced, so no change in how they run workflows |

**Everyone else**

| Platform Admins (human) | No Secrets Reader | Hold Secrets Reader (no access change until enforcement); shown in Roles & access and on the role's People tab |
| Platform Admin assigning Secrets Reader | 409 "can't be assigned yet" | Allowed, fixed boundaries |
| System accounts, external users, customer users, new users | — | Unchanged |

## Summary

Identities are ordinary user accounts that run work no person started (schedules, webhooks, events, endpoint keys). This change creates them and lets a workflow name the one it runs unattended as. **Nothing runs as an identity yet** — run lineage (next change) reads them.

- **`users.identity_kind`** marks an identity: `org_default` (one per organization, including the provider organization), `global_default` (one, with no organization) or `custom` (for later). Identities take role assignments like anyone else.
- **Migration `20261003_r3b_identities`** creates a default identity for every organization and the global identity (the users organization check is widened to allow it), and gives the provider organization's identity **Platform Admin** through an ordinary assignment. Every global workflow with an event subscription or an enabled endpoint gets `run_identity_id` = the provider organization's identity, which matches how those runs are treated today. Idempotent; the downgrade removes exactly what it created.
- **Creating an organization** — through the API or a git-sync import — creates its default identity in the same transaction.
- **Identities never sign in.** Every path that mints session tokens (password, MFA, passkey, device code, refresh, SSO, MCP OAuth) refuses them; SSO provisioning, registration and user creation refuse the reserved `identities.bifrost.internal` email domain.
- **Identities stay out of people management:** not in the Users list, user counts or first-user detection; update/delete through the people routes answer 409, bulk operations report them as per-user failures.
- **`workflows.run_identity_id`** (PATCH, CLI `--run-identity-id`, MCP `run_identity_id`, workflow response): an identity of the workflow's own organization; for a global or provider-organization workflow, the global identity or a provider-organization identity. Null = the organization's default identity. Every write that changes a workflow's organization (PATCH, re-registration, git-sync pull) re-checks it. It is environment-specific and not written to the manifest; git-sync and deploy leave it in place.
- **`users.organization_id` now follows its organization's id** (`ON UPDATE CASCADE`), so git sync can still re-key an organization matched by name across environments now that every organization has an account.

## Before / after

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Any workflow, form, app, agent or trigger run | — | Unchanged (scenario matrix unchanged, `pre_r3b.py` untouched) |
| Users list, counts, first-user setup | — | Unchanged (identities excluded) |
| Organizations | No accounts created | Each has a default identity, created with it |
| Platform Admin role holders | People only | Also the provider organization's identity (shows on the role's People tab) |
| Global workflows with a subscription or enabled endpoint | — | Name the provider organization's identity (`run_identity_id`; not read yet) |
| Sign-in / register with an identity email | — | 401 |
| Create a person on `@identities.bifrost.internal` | Allowed | 422 |
| PATCH / delete an identity via `/api/users/{id}` | — | 409 "Identities are managed from Identities" |
| Git sync re-keying an organization matched by name | Refused when the organization had any account | Its accounts follow it |

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `./test.sh quality api` | clean |
| `./test.sh unit` (full; contract fingerprint refreshed for the additive field) | 8096 passed |
| `./test.sh e2e` (full backend, before review fixes) | 2119 passed, 1 error (round-trip cleanup — fixed in this PR) |
| After review fixes: git sync, round-trip, workspace bundle import, workflows, organizations, auth, users, identity/run-identity tests, scenario matrix, all migration rehearsals | green |
| `client`: `npm run tsc`, `npm run lint`; `v1.d.ts` regenerated | clean |
| Debug-stack drive (CLI + REST): new organization gets its identity; Users list has none; identity sign-in/register refused; reserved domain refused; `bifrost workflows update --run-identity-id` sets an allowed identity and refuses a disallowed one | as expected |

New tests: `test_r3b_identities_migration_rehearsal.py`, `test_identities_service.py`, `test_identity_accounts.py`, `test_workflow_run_identity.py`, plus git-sync organization/workflow import cases.

## Post-deploy check

Identity count per organization (one each, plus one global); provider identity holds Platform Admin; count of global workflows naming it; every identity's `last_login` is NULL; API error classes unchanged.
