prs.title: Runs record who they run for: run user, starter and root execution
prs.body:
## Summary

Every run now records who it runs for. Each execution gets `run_user_id`, `started_by_user_id` and `root_execution_id`; each agent run gets `run_user_id`. **Nothing reads these for a decision yet**: authorization, scope, the SDK-visible identity (`context.user_id`, `is_platform_admin`), `executed_by` and error behaviour are unchanged. The next change observes against them.

- **One module decides lineage** where a run starts: `shared/run_lineage.py`.
  - A person (REST, CLI, web SDK, app, form, data provider, MCP, chat, integration test run, delayed run): the person. An admin's `run_as` changes the acting user, not the run user.
  - A child run (engine token): copied from the parent execution, so a whole tree keeps the starter's user and the first run's id as root. A parent that recorded no lineage (started before deploy) gives its child none.
  - Schedule, webhook, topic, endpoint key: the workflow's `run_identity_id`, otherwise its organization's default identity; a global workflow uses the global identity.
  - Anonymous or embedded form/app, service: the default identity of that form's or app's organization (global identity when it has none).
- **Transport.** Every enqueue/run function takes a required keyword-only `lineage`. The pending record carries it to the consumer, which writes it on the row. The engine token gets attribution-only claims (`engine_run_user_id`, `engine_started_by_user_id`, `engine_root_execution_id`). Delayed rows store it at insert and the promoter forwards it. A pending record written before deploy (no `lineage` key) is consumed as before, with no lineage recorded.
- **Agent runs** record their run user:
  - API, rerun, chat, SDK and MCP gateway runs: the caller.
  - Event-started runs: the agent organization's identity.
  - Delegated runs: the delegating run's user.
  - Workflow tool calls run for the agent run's user.
- **Migration `20261004_r3b_lineage`**:
  - Nullable columns with no defaults; existing rows stay NULL.
  - Foreign keys `ON DELETE SET NULL` added `NOT VALID`, so adding them doesn't scan the 4 GB `executions` table.
  - Partial indexes (`IS NOT NULL`) built `CONCURRENTLY`, so deleting a user doesn't scan `executions`.
- **Also included:**
  - `IdentityKind` moves to `src.models.enums`, so the worker and scheduler import lineage without fastapi.
  - The webhook protocol imports starlette's `Request` for typing only. This fixes `test_import_hygiene::test_scheduler_closure_has_no_heavyweights`, which already failed on main; it is slow-marked, so the PR lane doesn't run it.
  - The scenario matrix gains `test_every_run_records_its_lineage`, and its world gives the global probe the provider organization's identity, as the identities migration does.

## Before / after

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Any run's behaviour, access, scope, SDK identity, `executed_by` | — | Unchanged (scenario matrix unchanged, `pre_r3b.py` untouched) |
| `executions` row | `executed_by` only | + run user, starter, root execution |
| `agent_runs` row | `caller_user_id` (string) | + `run_user_id` |
| Engine token | `engine_caller_*` attribution | + `engine_run_user_id`, `engine_started_by_user_id`, `engine_root_execution_id` (attribution only) |
| Deleting a user | Nulls `executed_by` (indexed) | Also nulls the lineage columns (partial indexes) |

## Not in this change

- No `cause_user_id`. Events don't record who emitted them yet; that capture and the column come with the observers.
- No backfill. Existing rows, including the delayed row pending in production, keep NULL lineage.
- Agent system tools that call the REST API through the MCP bridge record that token's account. That is the caller when a person started the agent, and the system account for event-started agent runs. Carrying the agent run's identity through the bridge needs a principal claim reader, which comes with the observers.
- `rule.REACH` / `pre_r3b.py` are unchanged; the reach expectations move with the observers.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `./test.sh quality api` | 0 errors, ruff clean |
| `./test.sh unit` | 8124 passed |
| `./test.sh e2e` (full, before the final review fixes) | 2125 passed |
| After the review fixes: `tests/e2e/scenarios/`, `test_agent_delegation_lifecycle.py`, `test_run_lineage_anonymous.py`, `test_mcp_endpoints.py`, `test_r3b_lineage_migration_rehearsal.py`, `tests/unit/services/mcp_server/` | all passed |
| `tests/unit/test_import_hygiene.py` (slow) | 4 passed |
| Matrix mutation (child lineage removed) | `test_every_run_records_its_lineage` fails on every child and grandchild |
| Live drive (debug stack) | person → child → grandchild: all one run user and one root; `executed_by` of the children unchanged; a delayed run, once promoted, records the person, rooted at itself |
| Missed-start check (one-off pyright with `reportCallIssue=error`) | no missing `lineage` arguments; the remaining call errors already exist on main |
| Production read-only probe | every organization (94) has a default identity, one global identity, one delayed row pending |

## Problem

The V2 App scaffold's starter "Run workflow" button called a sample workflow by default (`functions/hello.py::main` in a Solution, rewritten to `workflows/hello.py::main` for `bifrost app create`). An independent App's instance has no such workflow, so the first click returned 404.

- **Solution scaffold**: no longer writes `functions/hello.py` or its `.bifrost/workflows.yaml` entry. The workflow existed only to back the button. Without a caller, every scaffolded Solution, and every `migrate-app` run since it shares `_scaffold_app`, would deploy an unused `hello` workflow into each install. Removed along with `_SAMPLE_WORKFLOW_*` and the "Sample workflow at ..." output.

```tsx
const wf = useWorkflowMutation<{ message: string }>("functions/hello.py::main");
<button onClick={() => wf.mutate({})} disabled={wf.loading}>Run workflow</button>
```
plus `functions/hello.py` + a `workflows.yaml` entry in Solution workspaces.

prs.title: App SDK header: one row with a menu button on phones, nav prop
prs.body:
## Summary

Two changes to `BifrostHeader` (the web SDK, `client/src/lib/app-sdk/bifrost-header.tsx`): it stays on one row on phones, and it can render the app's navigation through a new optional `nav` prop.

**Phones (below 640px).** The header is one row in the navigation-drawer layout (as in Gmail, GitHub and Material): a menu button on the left (`aria-label="Open menu"`, `aria-expanded`), then the truncated title, and nothing else. The button opens a panel under the header with:
- "Back to Bifrost" (first item; it leaves the bar on phones)
- the nav links
- the `action` slot
- the theme toggle (when `supportsTheme`)
- the account section: name, email, Log out

Without `nav`, the panel still holds Back to Bifrost, the theme toggle and the account section.

The panel is a full-width sheet hanging from the bar, not a full-height left drawer. At 390px a drawer would cover most of the screen anyway. The sheet keeps the bar visible, so the button in the top-left corner stays the close control (it shows an X). Its height fits its contents.

Accessibility and closing:
- The panel is `role="dialog"` labelled "Menu".
- Focus moves to its first control and Tab cycles inside it.
- Escape closes it and returns focus to the menu button.
- It also closes on a backdrop tap, on following a link, on browser back/forward, and when the viewport crosses the breakpoint.

The breakpoint is read with `matchMedia` (`useSyncExternalStore`), so phones never mount the wide controls. The `action` slot therefore renders in exactly one place.

**`nav` prop.** `nav={{ items: [{ label, to, end? }], link: NavLink }}`.
- The SDK stays router-free: its only peer dependencies are react, react-dom and lucide-react. The app passes its router's link component, and react-router's `NavLink` fits the `BifrostNavLinkProps` contract as-is. The vitest file passes the real `NavLink`, so tsc checks that.
- Active state comes from the `aria-current="page"` the router sets. The header's scoped stylesheet styles it: foreground text and underline on wide screens, an accent background on phones.
- New exported types: `BifrostHeaderNav`, `BifrostNavItem`, `BifrostNavLinkProps`.

**Desktop: the links render as a tab row inside the header, under the title bar, not inline in the bar.** Reasons:
- It keeps the #896 shell's look and still fits long titles and five or more sections (the row scrolls horizontally).
- Inline links would compete with the title and controls for one row and force a second truncation rule.
- The app has one nav list, and one component renders it at both widths.

**Scaffold.** `_v2_scaffold_files` `app_tsx`, which `bifrost app create` reuses, now passes `NAV` through `nav` instead of rendering its own `NavLink` row. The `cn` import was only used by that row, so it is gone. The scaffold tests are updated, rebased on #897.

**Docs.**
- The build skill's `best-practices/apps.md` and `references/web-sdk-v2.md` now describe the prop and the phone layout.
- `generated/web-sdk-surface.md` is regenerated.
- The mirrors are synced with `scripts/sync-codex-skills.sh`.

**Light-theme contrast.** I re-measured the "low contrast" I reported earlier on the active nav link and the primary button. Once the theme transition finishes, the computed colours are correct: foreground `oklch(0.145 0 0)` for the active link, `oklch(0.985 0 0)` text on `oklch(0.38 0.09 220)` for the button. My earlier screenshots were taken mid-way through the 0.12–0.15s colour transition after a theme toggle. There was nothing to fix, so no colours changed. The new screenshots wait for transitions to settle.

The change is compatible: `sdk-contract.json` is untouched and no SDK file was added, so the Dockerfile SDK lists are unchanged.

## Before / after

Measured on a deployed V2 App titled "Service Desk Operations Dashboard", headless Chromium, light and dark:

| Viewport | Before (main) | After |
|---|---|---|
| 390px | Two rows (82px): title, then theme toggle, avatar, name and chevron wrapped below; separate nav row under that | One row (46px): `☰  Service Desk Operations Dashboard` (the title truncates when longer); no nav row |
| 390px, menu open | — | Full-width panel (320px): ← Back to Bifrost · Home (active), About · Dark/Light mode · avatar, name, email · Log out; backdrop dims the page; focus on "Back to Bifrost"; tapping About goes to `/about` and closes the panel |
| 1280px | Title bar (51px) + the scaffold's own nav row | Same title bar + the header's tab row (90px total); Home underlined |

prs.title: Report-only access checks in the audit log (R3b 2c)
prs.body:
Every run is now checked, report-only, against the managed-identity model: for each call a run makes, the server works out what the model would decide (the run user's reach, plus what the workflow adds) next to what today's code decides, and writes to the audit log everything Phase 2 enforcement could change: every call the model would block, every move into another organization, and every `run_as`, policy and secret decision. Allowed calls inside the run user's own organization or Global, and denials today's code already makes, are not written because enforcement cannot change them. **Nothing changes what any request does**; today's code still decides everything.

## What it records

`access.check` audit events, outcome `success` / `failure` (`failure` = the model would block it), `details.enforced = false`, with the run user, workflow, route, target and a step-by-step trace:

| Check | Written when |
|---|---|
| Org a call acts in (tables, config, integrations, knowledge, files, lists) | the model would block it, or it acts in another organization |
| Child run placement, `run_as` of another user | blocked, or always for `run_as` |
| Entry (an agent run nobody started opening a workflow or its agent) | the model would block it |
| Table and file policies (judged with the run user's own roles and claims; admin predicate = Platform Admin or Full workflow) | the model would block what today allows, or a policy decision is made |
| Secret reads (kind and name, never the value) | always |

Each decision is written once per run. Calls the engine makes without run lineage, and checks that cannot be judged, are written as `access.check_gap` with a reason. Judging happens after the response is sent; policy checks run in a savepoint; a failure in any of it is logged and never reaches the request.

## Also in this PR
- The principal reads the run-lineage claims; the MCP REST bridge carries the run user of an agent nobody started (its system-tool child runs no longer record the system account).
- `GET /api/audit?group_by=workflow|action|resource_type|outcome|user|organization` returns counts and the newest entry per group. **Access change:** holders of `roleassignments.read` (Platform Operators, at customer organizations) can read `access.check` events in the organizations that permission reaches; everything else in the audit log stays Platform Admin only.
- Identity matrix: Global is in every reach. PRE_R3B: 46 cells leave (now match the rule), 67 join (today's SDK refuses a customer run's explicit Global target), 233 → 254. A new test checks that blocking exactly what the checks flag yields the rule, per route. Scenario staff hold the Platform Operator role, as production staff do.

## Before / after

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request behaviour | — | unchanged |
| Audit log | no access checks | `access.check` / `access.check_gap` events for runs |
| `/api/audit` | Platform Admins | Platform Admins; Operators read access checks in their reach; `group_by` |
| Agent system-tool child runs (agent nobody started) | run user = system account | run user = the agent's organization identity |

## Tests

prs.title: Sweep agent runs stuck in cancelling
prs.body:
## Problem
Cancelling an agent run sets it to `cancelling` and relies on the worker to finish it. If the worker is gone, nothing ever completes the run: the stuck-run sweeper only handled `queued` and `running` agent runs. Production has agent runs that have sat in `cancelling` for over a month.

## Change
- The sweeper that already handles stuck workflow executions (every 5 minutes) now also marks agent runs `cancelled` once they have been in `cancelling` for 3 minutes (`CANCELLING_TIMEOUT_MINUTES`, the same rule as workflow executions). Chat runs get the same `cancelled` chat event the worker sends.
- The time is measured from when cancellation was requested, not from when the run started. Otherwise a long run cancelled seconds ago could be swept while its worker is still winding down; the worker's final write (partial output, tokens, duration) would then be skipped. New column `agent_runs.cancel_requested_at`, set by both cancel paths (`POST /api/agent-runs/{id}/cancel` and chat cancel).
- Migration `20261004_agent_run_cancel_req_at` adds the column and backfills runs already in `cancelling` with `coalesce(started_at, created_at)`, so they are swept on the first pass after deploy.

prs.title: Audit retention: archive to object storage, verify, then clear
prs.body:
## What this does
Audit events no longer grow Postgres without limit. Admins set two windows in **Settings → Maintenance → Audit Retention**:
- **Keep in database:** events older than this move to an archive in object storage. The default is 90 days.
- **Keep in archive:** archived events older than this are deleted. The default is 365 days, and "Keep archives forever" is available.

Both ages are measured from when the event happened. One rule applies to every audit event, `access.check` included.

**Archive first, verify, then clear.** A row leaves Postgres only after it has been written to storage, read back, and verified (checksum, count, exact ids in order). The delete happens in the same short transaction that records the archived file in a catalog, and that transaction holds the job's current lease.

## Defaults
- **Existing installs:** the migration finds audit events already present and sets 90 days in the database and an unlimited archive. Nothing is ever deleted from the archive unless an admin changes that.
- **New installs:** 90 days in the database, 365 days in the archive.

## How it works
- **Daily job.** `audit.archive` is a PlatformJob that runs at 02:30 UTC (Run now and Preview are also available). It works through batches oldest first (at most 5,000 rows or about 64 MB per batch). Each batch is grouped per organization (or Global) and UTC day. Each group is written as deterministic JSONL.gz to `_audit/v1/org=<uuid|global>/day=<YYYY-MM-DD>/<sha256>.jsonl.gz`, read back and verified, and only then deleted. Each archived line includes a snapshot of the actor and organization names at archive time.
- **Restart safety.** The job freezes its windows in a checkpoint, so a retry continues with the same windows. The same rows always produce the same file name, so a rerun after a crash is safe.
- **Expiry.** Archived files are deleted page by page, inside a transaction that holds the lease.
- **Catalog.** `audit_archive_segments` records one row per archived file (no foreign keys, so archives outlive organizations).
- **New index.** `ix_audit_logs_created_id (created_at, id)`, built `CONCURRENTLY`.
- **Export (recovery).** `POST /api/audit/exports` runs an `audit.query` PlatformJob that combines archived and current events into one JSONL.gz file. It is downloaded from `GET /api/audit/exports/{job_id}/download`. The access rules are the same as the audit page:
  - Platform Admins can export everything.
  - Holders of `roleassignments.read` can export only `access.check*` events in the organizations they reach.
  - Access is checked when the export is requested, inside the job, and again at download.
  - Downloads expire after 7 days.
  - Archive and export share one lock and never run at the same time.
- **Audit page.** `GET /api/audit` now states its window to Platform Admins: "Showing events since …; older events are archived through …", with an Export button.
- **Preview.** Preview, and the confirmation shown when shortening the archive window, report exactly what would be archived and deleted. That includes events already past the archive window, which are archived and removed in the same run.
- **Runbook.** `docs/runbooks/audit-retention.md`.

## Deviations from the design, stated
- Export cleanup runs inside the daily archive job rather than as a separate hourly schedule.
- The Playwright happy path covers the card and Preview. Settings changes, the shortening confirmation and export are covered by vitest and backend e2e.
- `OrgReach` moved from `authorization/enforce.py` to `authorization/reach.py` so the scheduler doesn't import FastAPI (import hygiene). The class is unchanged.
- Leftover files: if an upload succeeds but its commit fails, and the rows change before the next run, the uploaded file stays in storage with no catalog row. It is ignored and never swept, because deleting after a failed commit is unsafe (the commit may have succeeded with the reply lost). This is documented in the runbook.

## Verification
- Full `./test.sh e2e`: 2158 passed, 0 failed (24.5 min)
- Focused backend tests: archiver (real Postgres + SeaweedFS: crash, corruption, stale lease, delete mismatch, expiry, storage unavailable), job handler unit tests, retention API, export (tenant isolation across archived and current rows, lost access, missing file), audit list, deny probe, decision matrix, access list, contract/DTO tripwires, org-scoping enforcement, alembic single head.
- `./test.sh quality api`: clean. `npm run tsc` clean, `npm run lint` 0 errors.
- vitest: service, settings card, banner, export dialog, AuditLogPage, Maintenance, Settings.
- Playwright: `e2e/audit-retention.admin.spec.ts`.
- Live drive on a port-mode debug stack: seeded old events, Preview, Run now (rows archived and catalogued), the shorten dialog showing the exact count, Cancel restoring the field, the banner, and an export downloaded with snapshot names. Screenshots in light, dark, desktop and phone width were sent for UX review.
- Not run locally: full vitest, full Playwright, `./test.sh pre-pr` (the merge queue runs them).

prs.title: Run and event retention: delete finished runs after a window, keep cost history
prs.body:
## What this does
Finished runs and events no longer pile up in Postgres forever. Admins set one window in **Settings → Maintenance → Run history**: **30 days** by default, from 30 to 3650 days, or "Keep forever". It applies to new and existing installs alike. A daily job deletes:
- finished workflow runs: Success, Failed, Timeout, Cancelled, CompletedWithErrors and Stuck, counted from `completed_at`. Their logs go with them.
- finished agent runs and their steps: completed, failed, budget_exceeded, timeout and cancelled. Verdict history and flag conversations go with them.
- events (and their deliveries) older than the window. This replaces the hard-coded 30-day purge in `event_cleanup`, which is removed. Stuck-delivery cleanup stays.

These are never deleted: Scheduled, Pending, Running, Cancelling or paused runs, and any agent run that still has a child run. There is no archive; audit is the durable record.

## Cost and resource history is kept
**The rule:** every finished workflow run is counted exactly once. While it is kept, it is counted in `executions`. After it is deleted, it is counted in the new `workflow_run_daily` table. The daily row covers the run's day, org, workflow, name and status: run count, duration, CPU, peak cores/RSS/memory, AI cost and AI calls.
- **Same transaction.** The job writes the rollup in the same transaction that deletes the run. A crash therefore cannot lose a run or count it twice.
- **No hot path, no backfill.** Nothing writes the table outside the job, and no backfill is needed. With "Keep forever" the table stays empty.
- **AI usage rows outlive their runs.** The `ai_usage` foreign keys to `executions` and `agent_runs` are dropped. The ids stay as plain values, like `audit_logs.execution_id`. Just before a run is deleted, the job stamps `ai_usage.workflow_id` and `ai_usage.agent_id`. A side effect: deleting an agent no longer deletes its AI cost rows.
- **Reports read one source,** `workflow_run_source` (kept runs plus the rollup):
  - usage report summary and per-workflow CPU/memory;
  - by-workflow and by-agent AI cost;
  - the workflow resource report's **workflows view**, whose window now goes up to 366 days. The runs view still lists only kept runs, with a 31-day window.
  - all-time execution totals;
  - `/api/metrics/workflows`.
- **Tests:** e2e tests assert identical totals before and after deletion.
- **Dead columns dropped:** `execution_metrics_daily.total_ai_*` was never written.

## How it works
- **Daily job.** `run.retention` is a PlatformJob that runs at 03:00 UTC; Preview (dry run) and Run now are also available.
  - It deletes oldest first, in short batches: 1,000 workflow runs, 500 agent runs, 1,000 events.
  - Each batch holds the job's lease row lock, so a stale runner deletes nothing.
  - Each batch deletes exactly the selected ids. A count mismatch rolls the batch back.
  - It removes at most 100,000 rows per table per run, so a large first backlog is spread over several nights (shown as "continues tomorrow").
  - The cutoff is frozen in the checkpoint, so a retry deletes what the first attempt would have.
- **Agent runs are deleted leaves first.** The `parent_run_id` cascade therefore never removes a child.
- **Removed runs say so.**
  - **API:** 404 detail text for executions and agent runs (REST and the MCP gateway) now ends with "Finished runs are removed after N days." The status codes are unchanged.
  - **Client:** `useExecution` no longer polls a missing run every 2 s forever.
    - The run page and agent run page show "This run isn't available. Finished runs are removed after N days (retention)…" instead of an error with Retry.
    - Chat tool cards fall back to the recorded tool result.
    - Agent timeline rows show "Removed after N days (retention)".
  - **Public endpoint:** `GET /api/run-retention` returns `{days}` for this wording.
- **Migration** `20261006_run_retention`:
  - adds `workflow_run_daily`;
  - drops the two `ai_usage` FKs, with `lock_timeout` 5 s because the drop takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `executions` / `agent_runs`;
  - adds the stamp columns;
  - drops the dead columns;
  - builds `(completed_at, id)` indexes on `executions` and `agent_runs` `CONCURRENTLY`, without `IF NOT EXISTS`.
- **Runbook:** `docs/runbooks/run-retention.md`. It covers half-migrated recovery and states that downgrade drops `ai_usage` rows of deleted runs.

## Production rollout
- No setting row exists, so prod gets 30 days. About 392k finished workflow runs and 12.9k agent runs are past 30 days; the backlog clears over about 4 nights.
- `executions` is 4 GB. Autovacuum makes the freed space reusable but does not shrink the files. Reclaiming the space is a separate, manual `pg_repack` decision.

## Deviations from the design, stated
- **FKs dropped, not set to NULL.** The `ai_usage` → run FKs are dropped instead of switched to `ON DELETE SET NULL`. That keeps run counts and source filters working unchanged, and the context check constraint keeps working too.
- **Rollup written at deletion, not at completion.** More than 20 code paths finish a run; deletion is one exact place.
- **Dropped inline runs merge.** In the usage report's by-workflow list, inline runs that are kept keep their own named rows. Deleted inline runs merge into "Inline or deleted workflow".
- **Small metrics change.** `/api/metrics/workflows` (no client caller) now windows on `started_at` (or `completed_at` for runs that never started), not `created_at`. Its averages count only runs that have the value.

## Verification
- Full `./test.sh unit`: 8293 passed, 0 failed. Full `./test.sh e2e`: 2183 passed, 0 failed (24.6 min). Both ran on the final head.
- Focused backend tests:
  - deleter against real Postgres: rollup, stamping, leaf-first agent deletion, stale lease, mismatch;
  - history-source before/after equality: usage report, resource report with status filter, inline runs, never-started runs, UTC day boundary;
  - job handler unit tests;
  - retention API: settings, preview, real run, `info` / `last_run`, 404 text, authorization;
  - migration catalog checks;
  - generators: access list, operation inventory, openapi digest;
  - deny probe;
  - contract/DTO tripwires.
- `./test.sh quality api` is clean. `npm run tsc` is clean and `npm run lint` has 0 errors. Full vitest: 544 files, 3455 tests passed.
- Playwright: `e2e/run-retention.admin.spec.ts`, plus `e2e/audit-retention.admin.spec.ts`, now scoped to its own card.
- Live drive on a port-mode debug stack with synthetic data (12,345 old runs, 210 agent runs, 4,000 events):
  - the shorten dialog showed exact counts;
  - Preview worked;
  - Run now deleted 12,345 / 210 / 4,000 and rolled up 12,345 runs;
  - the removed-run page rendered correctly.
  - Screenshots in light and dark, at desktop and phone width, were sent for UX review.

**UX approval is needed before merge.**

Bumps the python-minor-and-patch group with 2 updates: [pydantic-ai-slim](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai) and [pydantic-ai-harness](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai). Updates `pydantic-ai-slim` from 2.50.0 to 2.53.0
Release notes

Sourced from pydantic-ai-slim's releases.

v2.53.0 (2026-10-01)

🛡️ Security

This release fixes one security issue in ConcurrencyLimitedModel. See the advisory for full details and affected versions.

  • GHSA-6fqq-452j-qhrp (high): a streamed request through ConcurrencyLimitedModel or limit_model_concurrency could keep its concurrency slot when the slot was released on a different task than the one that acquired it: after an early exit (the consumer stopped iterating, raised, or was cancelled), and also after fully consuming stream_text() with its default debouncing. Repeated streams could then block every request sharing the limiter. Agent-level max_concurrency and non-streaming requests are not affected. Reported by @​lche511. (#9478)

The fix also changes how limiters are shared: a model wrapper now raises UserError when it shares a limiter with the agent making the request or with an enclosing model wrapper, ConcurrencyLimiter.acquire() takes a slot on every call, even on the same task, and a custom AbstractConcurrencyLimiter must allow release() from another task.

Patched in 2.53.0. v1 is not affected.

What's Changed

⚠️ Compatibility Notes

  • Add oneOf schema support to TestModel's generated data by @​pydanty in pydantic/pydantic-ai#8783

Updates `@tiptap/extension-link` from 3.31.3 to 3.31.4
Release notes

Sourced from @​tiptap/extension-link's releases.

v3.31.4

@​tiptap/extension-mathematics

Patch Changes

  • The mathematics extension no longer crashes the editor in older WebKit browsers and WKWebView.

@​tiptap/core

Patch Changes

  • Fix a TypeError thrown when the source editor is destroyed right after dragging content into another editor.
  • splitBlock no longer throws TransformError: Inserted content deeper than insertion position when the selection spans block boundaries (for example from the start of one paragraph into another block, or across an isolating node). The command now returns false when the split is not possible.
  • Prevent extra CSS declarations from being rendered from editor content.
  • Atom block directives (:::name {…} :::) indented by up to 3 spaces are now tokenized, matching CommonMark indentation rules for block constructs.
  • Numeric HTML entities (&[#39](https://github.com/ueberdosis/tiptap/tree/HEAD/packages/extension-link/issues/39);, ') are now decoded when parsing markdown, instead of showing up as literal text in the editor.
  • The editor element keeps role="textbox" after setOptions() when editorProps.attributes is set. Before, a re-render in React replaced the default role with the user attributes. Attributes passed as a function now get the default role as well.
  • Undoing an input rule restores the Markdown characters that triggered it when using Collaboration.
  • Bind parseMarkdown and renderMarkdown to the configured extension so hooks can read this.options and this.name without an Editor.
  • Pressing Enter before the text of a checked task item now leaves the new empty item unchecked and the item with the text checked. Attributes declared with keepOnSplit: false now reset on the new item, not on the one that keeps the text.
  • Stop joinItemForward and joinItemBackward from joining across isolating nodes.
  • Node views without a contentDOM no longer ignore selection mutations, so ProseMirror moves the caret back to a valid position when the browser places it inside the node view.

@​tiptap/markdown

Patch Changes

  • Fix Markdown serialization of inline code containing backticks
  • Bind parseMarkdown and renderMarkdown to the configured extension so hooks can read this.options and this.name without an Editor.

@​tiptap/extension-code

Patch Changes

  • Fix Markdown serialization of inline code containing backticks

@​tiptap/extension-table

Patch Changes

  • Table cells exported to Markdown now escape literal pipe characters, so the cell content survives when the output is read back.
  • Multi-block table cells no longer leak a U+001F control character into Markdown.
  • Right-clicking a cell inside a multi-cell table selection no longer collapses that selection.
  • Prevent extra CSS declarations from being rendered from editor content.
  • Table cells and headers no longer render the default colspan="1" and rowspan="1" attributes. Cells that actually span still render them, matching how prosemirror-tables serializes spans.

@​tiptap/extension-list

Patch Changes

prs.title: feat(sdk): add branding and organization hooks
prs.body:
V2 apps can now read platform branding and caller-visible organizations directly through the SDK, removing the need to distribute workflows that wrap those platform reads.

`useBranding()` exposes logo URLs, the application name, and light/dark palettes, and applies the same CSS variables as the main client by default. Logo URLs resolve against the provider API URL for external development. `useOrganizations()` supports deferred loading, inactive organizations, explicit errors, and refetching while preserving the endpoint's authorization. Both hooks discard stale responses when scope or credentials change. The provider now keeps its authenticated fetch stable across theme changes so switching themes preserves loaded data.

The main client and SDK share the branding palette and CSS implementation. Production/dev SDK packaging, the compatible wire-surface snapshot, generated SDK reference, build skill guidance, and plugin mirrors are updated. No breaking wire-contract version bump is needed. Existing apps pick up the hooks through an SDK update or redeploy; installed plugins receive the guidance in the next versioned release.

Validation:
- `./test.sh client unit src/lib/app-sdk src/lib/branding.test.ts` — 239 passed.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_sdk_package.py tests/unit/test_sdk_package_fingerprint.py tests/unit/test_skill_appendix_fresh.py -v` — 14 passed.
- `./test.sh tests/unit/test_skill_examples.py tests/unit/test_skill_appendix_fresh.py -v` — 10 passed.
- `./test.sh client e2e e2e/sdk-platform-hooks.admin.spec.ts` — setup and the packaged SDK happy path passed. The feature test took 1.3 seconds and enqueues no platform jobs: it downloads the actual SDK tarball and verifies organization data plus light/dark button colors against live endpoints.
- `./test.sh quality api`, client `npm run tsc`, client `npm run lint`, and `python3 scripts/check_skill_mirrors.py` passed. Client lint has five existing warnings and no errors.

Full backend, client, and browser suites were not run locally; the merge queue runs the complete gate. An initial package check detected an old image-baked SDK; rebuilding the image and renewing the API's anonymous SDK volume resolved it, and the current package checks and browser test are green.

The operation surface inventory and SDK route count include both new hooks; organization listing no longer carries an SDK exclusion. The initial CI unit run exposed the stale inventory; it was reproduced locally and corrected.

Additional verification: `./test.sh tests/unit/services/test_operation_inventory.py tests/unit/services/test_operation_catalog.py -v` (14 passed), and `./test.sh quality api`.

prs.title: Explain access decisions: then vs now, what-if checks, and CLI
Person access page, Roles list and permission catalog (Effective Access)
prs.body:
## What this does
Admins can now see what a person can do, and where, on one page. Roles show what they grant, who holds them and where they apply. Nothing about enforcement changes.

- **Person page** (`/users/:userId`, tabs Access | Profile). It replaces the dialog that opened over the Users list.
  - **Header:** name, email, home organization and reach chips, plus a protected-account line when one applies. The ⋮ menu carries the same account actions as the list row: invites, Reset MFA, Sign Out of All Devices, Deactivate/Activate and Delete. Both places share one hook.
  - **Effective Access:** one row per place the person's roles reach (home, each placed org, All Customer Organizations, Global), with a column per permission area. Chips show the source role and place on hover or focus. A Platform Admin is one "All Permissions" chip.
  - **Role Assignments:** the editor now uses placement presets: Selected Organizations, All Customer Organizations, or All Organizations (= managed + provider org + Global). The presets offered are limited by the role and the caller.
    - A placement that matches no preset shows as Custom and is saved unchanged.
    - A role with a platform-wide permission placed on selected orgs gets a tappable warning.
  - **Quick edits:** the list row menu's Edit Profile still opens the dialog without leaving the list.
- **Roles list:** Built-in and Custom sections. Columns: grants (purple chips), holders, and where the role is placed (cyan chips).
- **Permission panel:** driven by the server's catalog, grouped by area and searchable. "Takes Effect with R3b" appears once per area that isn't enforced yet.
- **New routes:**
  - `GET /api/permissions/catalog`: every permission domain with Title Case name, area, actions, privileged permissions, scope (per organization / platform-wide / varies, derived from the access list), whether it's enforced, and display names. Readable by any signed-in user, because it's vocabulary only.
  - `GET /api/users/{id}/access`: the Effective Access map, gated exactly like the role-assignments read.
- **`RolePublic` gains** `holders`, `grants` and `placements`, computed only when consumer counts are (Platform Admins).
- **CLI:**
  - `bifrost permissions list`;
  - `bifrost users access <user>` (`users access check …` still works);
  - `bifrost users roles get <user>`;
  - `bifrost users roles set <user> [--base] [--role ROLE[=org:<ref>,customers,global,all]]… [--no-roles]`. `--base` alone keeps the current additional roles.
- **Shared pieces for PR 5:**
  - `--bf-reach*` and `--bf-power*` tokens, light and dark, with chip text at 5.47:1 or better;
  - a Badge `power` variant, plus `ReachChip`, `PermissionChip` and `GrantChip`;
  - a shared `EmptyState`;
  - the Badge warning variant moved to tokens.

## Copy rule (from review)
Display names follow Graph style in Title Case: Read / Read All / Read and Write, or the action's own verb (Run Workflows, Deploy Solutions). Everything that isn't a sentence is Title Case: buttons, headings, tabs, labels, badges, menu items. Sentences stay sentence case. The rule is written into `DESIGN.md`, with a one-line pointer in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

## Deviations, stated
- **`grants`, not `permissions`.** The new `RolePublic` field is named `grants`. R2b removed a free-form `permissions` dict from `RolePublic`, and older CLIs know that name with a different type.
- **Catalog gate.** The catalog is readable by any signed-in user rather than `roles.read`. Platform Operators can read access maps but not `roles.read@global`, and the map needs the catalog's areas.
- **Consumers column dropped** from the Roles list, to match the spec's columns. The counts are still on each role's tabs.
- **Test access lands in PR 5**, per spec §8.

## Verification
- On `3e6b085`: full `./test.sh unit` 8449 passed / 0 failed; full `./test.sh e2e` 2215 / 0. The Playwright specs for the changed journeys passed 15/15 (users, role-assignments, new user-access, roles detail, role lifecycle).
- After that, two client-only commits for chip styling and truncation: `./test.sh client unit` 561 files / 3595 tests passed, and the same Playwright specs 15/15 again, on the final head.
- `./test.sh quality api` is clean; `npm run tsc` is clean; `npm run lint` has 0 errors (5 existing warnings).

prs.title: Preserve completed evidence when agent delegation times out
prs.body:
When a specialist times out after completing diagnostic calls, its parent currently receives only a timeout error and can report those checks as never performed. Preserve a bounded receipt of captured tool results in the child run output and in the timeout error delivered to both autonomous and chat callers.

Receipts distinguish completed calls, failed calls, and unfinished operations, retain step/execution/child identifiers, and explicitly mark truncated or omitted evidence. Nested child receipts survive cancellation unwinding. The source is the executing child's own tool events and finalized descendants; tool arguments and its own model narrative are excluded. The durable error stays concise, and timeout/cancellation remain failure states. Existing delegation schemas, caller identity, organization boundaries, and successful output behavior are preserved.

The 600-second deadline remains. In the investigated read-only run, useful endpoint diagnostics were available at about 9m02s; a subsequent check was still running at the cutoff. Sequential checks, roughly 2m19s of orchestrator model time, and a rejected oversized-script preview explain the elapsed time. This evidence supports keeping the bounded deadline and preserving results, rather than increasing it. It does not establish an optimal deadline for every agent. Wall-clock wind-down policy is a separate follow-up.

Validation:
- `./test.sh tests/unit/services/test_autonomous_agent_executor.py tests/unit/services/test_agent_executor_tools.py -v`: 86 passed.
- `./test.sh tests/e2e/api/test_agent_delegation_lifecycle.py -v --durations=0`: 3 passed; new timeout persistence case took 0.13s excluding setup.
- Local replay of the captured incident: retained completed RMM, patch, and PowerShell facts and unfinished-call uncertainty; eight checks passed, 14,056 characters, zero external actions. Customer fixtures are not committed.
- `./test.sh pr-preflight`: passed repository consistency checks, API/client lint and types, 8,379 backend unit tests, 3,469 client tests, changed delegation E2E tests, and Python/JavaScript CodeQL (no findings on changed lines). Full preflight ran before updating to latest main; focused delegation tests and API quality checks were repeated after rebase.
- Full backend E2E and browser suites were not run locally; the merge queue remains the complete-suite gate.

Scope: in-process agent delegation shared by autonomous and chat callers. Independently queued MCP agent jobs and their root-run timeout are unchanged. Production deployment and representative live outcome verification remain pending.

Follow-up to #518.

The Product Updates content check must run validator code from trusted main, rather than from the PR being evaluated. Land the schema and deterministic validator before enabling that check in the feature PR. This also adds the image-bundle preparation entry point used by the upcoming runtime integration.

prs.title: Deliver in-app Product Updates with automatic durable acknowledgements
prs.body:
Product Updates now opens automatically for platform admins when their installed image contains approved entry UUIDs they have not seen. Opening the modal or history acknowledges the displayed batch; authenticated PostgreSQL receipts preserve that state across browsers, editorial changes, rollbacks and dev-to-stable promotion.

Help → Release Notes provides the permanent history path. Desktop/mobile share a scrollable feed, visible exit controls, concise feature cards, separate fix/hardening lists, verified feature screenshots and compact branded community links. Every image build packages the approved cumulative feed; formal GitHub release preparation separately filters the previous-full-release interval.

Validation: 22 focused client tests, TypeScript, ESLint, 37 tooling tests and shell release regressions passed. The production Docker-image browser journey passed, including a fresh-browser check that the modal does not repeat. Backend receipt/bundle tests cover authenticated ownership, hidden/unknown IDs and idempotent concurrent acknowledgement. The merge queue runs the broad suite; full suites were not run locally.

prs.title: Fix Product Updates validation in squash merge queues
prs.body:
Product Updates validation could not resolve PRs in a squash merge queue because a PR branch head is not an ancestor of GitHub's synthetic candidate. Resolve the exact candidate chain from GitHub's MergeQueueEntry head/base commit metadata, including batched entries, and reject incomplete or ambiguous scope.

This trusted-base helper must land before the Product Updates workflow in #918 consumes it. The workflow adapter changes remain in #918.

Validation: `node --test scripts/test_product_updates_scope.cjs` (8 passed); `git diff --check`. Tests cover the actual failed squash candidate, chained and batched entries, and missing/ambiguous/cyclic metadata. Broader suites are left to the merge queue.
